title.zh: 卷一百五十四 志第一百〇七 輿服六
title.raw: 卷一百五十四 志第一百〇七 輿服六 Volume 154 Treatises 107: Carriages and Clothes 6

sentences.zh: 輿服六○寶印符券宮室制度臣庶室屋制度

translations.literal: Carriages and Clothes 6 ○ Imperial Treasures, Seals, Tokens, Palace Regulations, Regulations on Subjects' Dwellings
translations.idiomatic: Carriages and Clothes 6: Imperial treasures and seals, tokens, palace regulations, and regulations governing the dwellings of subjects and commoners.

sentences.zh: 寶。

translations.literal: Treasures.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial treasures.

sentences.zh: 秦製，天子有六璽，又有傳國璽，歷代因之。

translations.literal: Under the Qin system, the Son of Heaven had six seals, and also the seal for transmitting the state; successive dynasties followed this.
translations.idiomatic: Under Qin institutions, the emperor possessed six imperial seals as well as the seal of dynastic transmission, and later dynasties preserved that practice.

sentences.zh: 唐改為寶，其制有八。

translations.literal: The Tang changed them to treasures; the system comprised eight.
translations.idiomatic: The Tang renamed them treasures and established a set of eight.

sentences.zh: 五代亂離，或多亡失。

translations.literal: During the chaos and disunion of the Five Dynasties, many were lost.
translations.idiomatic: Amid the turmoil of the Five Dynasties, many were lost or destroyed.

sentences.zh: 周廣順中，始造二寶：其一曰「皇帝承天受命之寶」，一曰「皇帝神寶」。

translations.literal: In the Guangshun era of Later Zhou, two treasures were first made: one inscribed "Treasure of the Emperor Receiving Mandate from Heaven," and one "Treasure of the Divine Emperor."
translations.idiomatic: In Later Zhou's Guangshun reign, the court first cast two treasures: one reading "Treasure of the Emperor Who Receives Heaven's Mandate," and another "Treasure of the Divine Emperor."

sentences.zh: 太祖受禪，傳此二寶，又製「大宋受命之寶」。

translations.literal: When Taizu received the abdication, he transmitted these two treasures and also made the "Treasure of the Great Song Receiving the Mandate."
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Taizu accepted the abdication, he inherited these two treasures and additionally commissioned the "Treasure of the Great Song's Received Mandate."

sentences.zh: 至太宗，又別製「承天受命之寶」。

translations.literal: By the time of Taizong, another was separately made: the "Treasure of Receiving Mandate from Heaven."
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Taizong, the court fashioned yet another treasure inscribed "Treasure of Receiving Mandate from Heaven."

sentences.zh: 是後，諸帝嗣服，皆自為一寶，以「 皇帝恭膺天命之寶」為文。

translations.literal: Thereafter, each succeeding emperor upon accession made a treasure of his own, with the inscription "Treasure of the Emperor Reverently Receiving Heaven's Mandate."
translations.idiomatic: Afterward, every new emperor on succeeding to the throne commissioned his own treasure bearing the text "Treasure of the Emperor Who Reverently Receives Heaven's Mandate."

sentences.zh: 凡上尊號，有司製玉寶，則以所上尊號為文。

translations.literal: Whenever an honorific title was bestowed, the responsible offices would make a jade treasure, using the honorific title as the inscription.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever the court bestowed an honorific title upon the emperor, the relevant offices would carve a jade treasure bearing that title as its inscription.

sentences.zh: 寶用玉，篆文，廣四寸九分，厚一寸二分。

translations.literal: Treasures were made of jade, in seal script, four cun nine fen wide and one cun two fen thick.
translations.idiomatic: The treasures were carved from jade in seal script, measuring four inches and nine tenths across and one inch and two tenths thick.

sentences.zh: 填以金盤龍鈕，係以暈錦大綬，赤小綬，連玉環；

translations.literal: They were set with a gold knob in the form of a coiled dragon, tied with a great cord of cloud-pattern brocade and a small red cord linked to jade rings;
translations.idiomatic: Each was fitted with a gold knob shaped as a coiled dragon, suspended from a great cord of cloud-pattern brocade and a shorter red cord joined to jade rings;

sentences.zh: 玉檢高七寸，廣二寸四分，厚四分；

translations.literal: the jade tablet was seven cun high, two cun four fen wide, and four fen thick;
translations.idiomatic: the accompanying jade tablet stood seven inches high, two inches and four tenths wide, and four tenths thick;

sentences.zh: 玉鬥方二寸四分，厚一寸二分：皆飾以紅錦，金裝，裹以紅錦，加紅羅泥金夾巴，納於小盝。

translations.literal: the jade cap was a square two cun four fen on a side and one cun two fen thick: all were adorned with red brocade and gold fittings, wrapped in red brocade, layered with red silk bearing gold mud and facing panels, and placed in a small casket.
translations.idiomatic: the jade cap-piece was a square two inches and four tenths on each side and one inch and two tenths thick; all these fittings were trimmed with red brocade and gold mountings, wrapped in red brocade, layered with gold-flecked red silk facing panels, and placed in a small casket.

sentences.zh: 盝以金裝，內設金床，暈錦褥，飾以雜色玻璃、碧石、珊瑚、金精石、瑪瑙。

translations.literal: The casket was gold-mounted, with a gold bed inside, a cloud-brocade cushion, and ornamentation of varicolored glass, green stone, coral, gold essence stone, and agate.
translations.idiomatic: The casket itself was gold-mounted; inside stood a gold bed with a cloud-pattern brocade cushion, embellished with varicolored glass, green stone, coral, gold-essence stone, and agate.

sentences.zh: 又盝二重，皆裝以金，覆以紅羅繡巴，載以腰輿及行馬，並飾以金。

translations.literal: There were also two further nested caskets, all gold-mounted, covered with embroidered red silk panels, borne on a waist litter and traveling horses, all trimmed with gold.
translations.idiomatic: Two additional nested caskets, likewise gold-mounted and covered with embroidered red silk panels, were carried on a waist litter and traveling horses, all adorned with gold.

sentences.zh: 又有香爐、寶子、香匙、灰匙、火箸、燭台、燭刀，皆以金為之，是所謂緣寶法物也。

translations.literal: There were also an incense burner, treasure box, incense spoon, ash spoon, fire tongs, candle stand, and candle knife, all made of gold—these are what are called the ritual objects accompanying the treasure.
translations.idiomatic: There were also an incense burner, treasure casket, incense spoon, ash spoon, fire tongs, candle stand, and candle knife, all of gold—these constituted the ritual paraphernalia accompanying the treasure.

sentences.zh: 別有三印：一曰「天下合同之印」，中書奏覆狀、流內銓曆任三代狀用之；

translations.literal: There were separately three seals: the first called "Seal of Universal Accord Under Heaven," used on memorial replies from the Secretariat, and on three-generation service records from the inner stream of the Board of Appointments;
translations.idiomatic: Three additional seals were kept: the first, the "Seal of Universal Accord Under Heaven," was used on memorial replies from the Secretariat and on three-generation service records from the inner stream of the Board of Appointments;

sentences.zh: 二曰「御前之印」，樞密院宣命及諸司奏狀內用之；

translations.literal: the second called "Seal of the Imperial Presence," used within edicts from the Bureau of Military Affairs and memorials from various offices;
translations.idiomatic: the second, the "Seal of the Imperial Presence," was used on orders from the Bureau of Military Affairs and on memorials submitted by the various offices;

sentences.zh: 三曰「書詔之印」，翰林詔敕用之。

translations.literal: the third called "Seal for Writing Imperial Edicts," used for edicts and commands from the Hanlin Academy.
translations.idiomatic: the third, the "Seal for Writing Imperial Edicts," was used for edicts and commands issued by the Hanlin Academy.

sentences.zh: 皆鑄以金，又以鍮石各鑄其一。

translations.literal: All were cast in gold, and one of each was also cast in brass.
translations.idiomatic: Each was cast in gold, and a duplicate of each was also cast in brass.

sentences.zh: 雍熙三年，並改為寶，別鑄以金，舊六印皆毀之。

translations.literal: In the third year of Yongxi, all were changed to treasures; new ones were separately cast in gold, and the old six seals were all destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of the Yongxi reign, all three were redesignated as treasures, newly cast in gold, and the former six seals were destroyed.

sentences.zh: 真宗即位，作皇帝受命寶，文曰「皇帝恭膺天命之寶」。

translations.literal: When Zhenzong acceded, he made the emperor's treasure of received mandate, inscribed "Treasure of the Emperor Reverently Receiving Heaven's Mandate."
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Zhenzong took the throne, he commissioned the emperor's treasure of received mandate, inscribed "Treasure of the Emperor Who Reverently Receives Heaven's Mandate."

sentences.zh: 大中祥符元年五月，詳定所言：「按玉牒、玉冊，用皇帝受命寶印之，納玉匱於石感，以天下同文之印封之。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the first year of Dazhong Xiangfu, the review office stated: "According to precedent, jade registers and jade volumes are impressed with the emperor's treasure of received mandate, the jade coffer is placed in a stone coffer, and it is sealed with the seal of universal script under heaven.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of the first year of Dazhong Xiangfu, the review office reported: "By precedent, jade registers and jade volumes are stamped with the emperor's treasure of received mandate, the jade coffer is placed within a stone coffer, and the seal of universal script under heaven is used to seal it.

sentences.zh: 今封禪泰山，請依舊制，別造玉寶一枚，方寸二分，文同受命寶。

translations.literal: Now, for the Fengshan at Mount Tai, we request that, following the old regulations, a separate jade treasure be made, two cun square, with the same inscription as the treasure of received mandate.
translations.idiomatic: For the forthcoming Fengshan rite at Mount Tai, we ask that, in accordance with former regulations, a separate jade treasure be made, two inches square, bearing the same inscription as the treasure of received mandate.

sentences.zh: 其封石感，用天下同文之印，舊史元無制度，今請用金鑄，大小同御前之寶，以『天下同文之寶』為文。

translations.literal: For sealing the stone coffer, the seal of universal script under heaven is to be used; the old histories contain no regulations for this; we now request that it be cast in gold, the same size as the treasure of the Imperial Presence, with the inscription "Treasure of Universal Script Under Heaven."
translations.idiomatic: To seal the stone coffer, the seal of universal script under heaven should be employed; since earlier histories prescribe no rule for this, we now request that it be cast in gold, matching the size of the treasure of the Imperial Presence, and inscribed "Treasure of Universal Script Under Heaven."

sentences.zh: 所有緣寶法物，亦請依式製造。」

translations.literal: All accompanying ritual objects for the treasure should also be manufactured according to the prescribed forms."
translations.idiomatic: All ritual paraphernalia accompanying the treasure should likewise be produced according to the prescribed specifications.

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: The request was approved.
translations.idiomatic: The court approved the proposal.

sentences.zh: 天禧元年十二月，召輔臣於滋福殿，觀新刻「五嶽聖帝玉寶』及「皇帝昭受乾符之寶」，命擇日迎導赴會靈觀奉安。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month of the first year of Tianxi, the emperor summoned chief ministers to the Hall of Nourishing Blessings to view the newly carved "Jade Treasures of the Sacred Emperors of the Five Marchmounts" and the "Treasure of the Emperor Who Manifestly Received the Qian Symbol," and ordered a day chosen to escort them in procession to the Temple of Assembled Spirits for enshrinement.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month of the first year of Tianxi, the emperor convened his chief ministers in the Hall of Nourishing Blessings to inspect the newly carved "Jade Treasures of the Sacred Emperors of the Five Marchmounts" and the "Treasure of the Emperor Who Manifestly Received the Qian Talisman," and directed that a date be chosen to escort them in procession to the Temple of Assembled Spirits for enshrinement.

sentences.zh: 其寶並金柙玉鈕，製作精妙。

translations.literal: These treasures all had gold frames and jade knobs; their workmanship was exquisitely refined.
translations.idiomatic: These treasures all bore gold frames and jade knobs, and their craftsmanship was extraordinarily fine.

sentences.zh: 真宗以奏章上帝，承前皆用御前之寶，以理未順，故改用昭受乾符之寶。

translations.literal: When Zhenzong presented memorials to the Supreme Lord, following precedent the Seal of the Imperial Presence had always been used; as this was not logically appropriate, he therefore changed to the Treasure of Manifestly Receiving the Qian Symbol.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Zhenzong addressed memorials to the Supreme Lord, earlier practice had always employed the Seal of the Imperial Presence; finding this inappropriate in principle, he substituted the Treasure of Manifestly Receiving the Qian Talisman.

sentences.zh: 嘉祐八年，仁宗崩，英宗立，翰林學士範鎮言：「伏聞大行皇帝受命寶及緣寶法物，與平生衣冠器用，皆欲舉而葬之，恐非所以稱先帝恭儉之意。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Jiayou, Renzong died and Yingzong succeeded; Hanlin academician Fan Zhen stated: "I have heard that the late emperor's treasure of received mandate and the ritual objects accompanying the treasure, together with the garments and implements used in his lifetime, are all to be buried with him; I fear this would not accord with the late emperor's spirit of reverent frugality.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year of Jiayou, after Emperor Renzong's death and Emperor Yingzong's accession, Hanlin academician Fan Zhen submitted: "I understand that the late emperor's treasure of received mandate, the ritual objects accompanying it, and the garments and implements he used in life are all to be interred with him; I fear this would not honor the late emperor's reputation for reverent frugality.

sentences.zh: 其受命寶，伏乞陛下自寶用之，且示有所傳付。

translations.literal: As for the treasure of received mandate, I humbly beg Your Majesty to keep and use it as your own treasure, thereby showing that succession has been transmitted.
translations.idiomatic: Regarding the treasure of received mandate, I respectfully urge Your Majesty to retain it and use it as your own, thereby demonstrating that the mandate has been duly transmitted.

sentences.zh: 若衣冠器玩，則請陳於陵寢及神御殿，歲時展視，以慰思慕。」

translations.literal: As for garments and ritual implements, I ask that they be displayed at the imperial tomb and in the spirit hall, to be viewed at the seasonal observances and to comfort those who yearn in remembrance."
translations.idiomatic: As for his garments and ritual implements, I propose that they be displayed at the imperial tomb precinct and in the spirit hall, to be viewed on the seasonal observances and to console those who mourn him.

sentences.zh: 詔檢討官考索典故，及命兩製、禮官詳議。

translations.literal: An edict ordered the review officials to search precedents and directed the two academies and the ritual offices to deliberate in detail.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered the review officials to search historical precedents and charged the two academies and the ritual offices to deliberate the matter in detail.

sentences.zh: 翰林學士王珪等奏曰：「受命寶者，猶昔傳國璽也，宜為天子傳器，不當改作。

translations.literal: Hanlin academician Wang Gui and others memorialized: "The treasure of received mandate is like the former seal for transmitting the state; it should be a treasure transmitted by the Son of Heaven and ought not to be remade.
translations.idiomatic: Hanlin academician Wang Gui and others memorialized: "The treasure of received mandate is analogous to the ancient seal for transmitting the state; it should remain the Son of Heaven's transmitted treasure and ought not to be recast.

sentences.zh: 古者藏先王衣服於廟寢，至於平生器玩，則前世既不皆納於方中，亦不盡陳於陵寢。

translations.literal: In antiquity the former kings' garments were stored in the temple dormitory; as for implements used in daily life, earlier ages neither placed them all in the central coffin nor displayed them all at the imperial tomb.
translations.idiomatic: In antiquity the deceased kings' garments were stored in the temple dormitory; as for objects used in daily life, earlier ages neither buried them all in the central coffin nor displayed them all at the imperial tomb.

sentences.zh: 謂今宜從省約，以稱先帝恭儉之實。」

translations.literal: We hold that the present case should follow economy, to accord with the late emperor's actual practice of reverent frugality."
translations.idiomatic: We believe the present case should follow a course of restraint, in keeping with the late emperor's genuine practice of reverent frugality.

sentences.zh: 帝不用其議，乃別造受命寶，命參知政事歐陽修篆文八字。

translations.literal: The emperor did not adopt their proposal but separately made a treasure of received mandate, ordering Associate Administrator Ouyang Xiu to compose the eight-character seal inscription.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor did not accept their proposal but commissioned a new treasure of received mandate, directing Associate Administrator Ouyang Xiu to compose its eight-character inscription.

sentences.zh: 至哲宗立，亦作焉，其文並同。

translations.literal: When Zhezong succeeded, one was also made, with the same inscription.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Zhezong acceded, he too had one made bearing the same inscription.

sentences.zh: 按所獻玉璽，色綠如藍，溫潤而澤，其文曰「受命於天，既壽永昌」。

translations.literal: According to the jade seal presented, its color was green like indigo, warm, moist, and lustrous; its inscription read "Having received mandate from Heaven, long life and eternal prosperity."
translations.idiomatic: Regarding the jade seal that was presented, its color was green as indigo, warm, moist, and lustrous, and its inscription read "Having received mandate from Heaven, long life and eternal prosperity."

sentences.zh: 其背螭鈕五盤，鈕間有小竅，用以貫組。

translations.literal: On its back was a chi knob with five coils; between the coils were small holes for threading the cord.
translations.idiomatic: On its reverse was a chi-dragon knob with five coils, and between the coils were small perforations for threading the cord.

sentences.zh: 又得玉螭首一，白如膏，亦溫潤，其背亦螭鈕五盤，鈕間亦有貫組小竅，其面無文，與璽大小相合。

translations.literal: A jade chi head was also obtained, white as fat, likewise warm and lustrous; its back also had a chi knob with five coils, and between the coils there were small holes for threading the cord; its face bore no inscription and matched the seal in size.
translations.idiomatic: A jade chi head was also recovered, white as tallow and equally warm and lustrous; its reverse likewise bore a chi knob with five coils and small holes for the cord between them; its face bore no inscription and matched the seal in size.

sentences.zh: 篆文工作，皆非近世所為。

translations.literal: The seal-script workmanship was none of what the recent age produces.
translations.idiomatic: The seal-script craftsmanship was clearly not the work of recent times.

sentences.zh: 臣等以歷代正史考之，璽之文曰「皇帝壽昌」者，晉璽也；

translations.literal: We, your ministers, examining the orthodox histories of successive dynasties, find that a seal whose inscription reads "Long life and prosperity for the emperor" was a Jin seal;
translations.idiomatic: Your ministers, examining the orthodox histories of successive dynasties, find that a seal inscribed "Long life and prosperity for the emperor" belonged to the Jin;

sentences.zh: 曰「受命於天」者，後魏璽也；

translations.literal: one reading "Having received mandate from Heaven" was a Later Wei seal;
translations.idiomatic: one reading "Having received mandate from Heaven" was a Later Wei seal;

sentences.zh: 「 有德者昌」，唐璽也；

translations.literal: "He of virtue shall prosper" was a Tang seal;
translations.idiomatic: "He of virtue shall prosper" was a Tang seal;

sentences.zh: 「惟德允昌」，石晉璽也；

translations.literal: "Only virtue ensures prosperity" was a Later Jin seal;
translations.idiomatic: "Only virtue ensures prosperity" was a Later Jin seal;

sentences.zh: 則「既壽永昌」者，秦璽可知。

translations.literal: thus "Long life and eternal prosperity" can be known to be the Qin seal.
translations.idiomatic: thus the phrase "long life and eternal prosperity" can be identified as the Qin seal.

sentences.zh: 今得璽於咸陽，其玉乃藍田之色，其篆與李斯小篆體合。

translations.literal: Now the seal has been obtained at Xianyang; its jade is of Lantian color, and its seal script matches the small seal script of Li Si.
translations.idiomatic: The seal has now been recovered at Xianyang; its jade is of Lantian hue, and its characters match the small seal script of Li Si.

sentences.zh: 飾以龍鳳鳥魚，乃蟲書鳥跡之法，於今所傳古書，莫可比擬，非漢以後所作明矣。

translations.literal: Ornamented with dragon, phoenix, bird, and fish, it follows the method of insect script and bird traces; among ancient books transmitted today nothing can compare with it—it is clearly not a work of post-Han times.
translations.idiomatic: Adorned with dragon, phoenix, bird, and fish motifs, it follows the method of insect script and bird traces; among ancient books extant today nothing can compare with it—it is plainly not a post-Han creation.

sentences.zh: 今陛下嗣守祖宗大寶，而神璽自出，其文曰「受命於天，既壽永昌」，則天之所畀，烏可忽哉？

translations.literal: Now Your Majesty continues to guard the great treasure of the ancestors, and this divine seal has appeared of itself; its inscription reads "Having received mandate from Heaven, long life and eternal prosperity"—how can what Heaven has bestowed be neglected?
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty now guards the great treasure of the ancestors, and this divine seal has emerged unbidden; its inscription reads "Having received mandate from Heaven, long life and eternal prosperity"—how can a gift bestowed by Heaven be disregarded?

sentences.zh: 漢、晉以來，得寶鼎瑞物，猶告廟改元，肆眚上壽，況傳國之器乎？

translations.literal: Since Han and Jin times, when precious cauldrons and auspicious objects were obtained, the court still announced them at the ancestral temple, changed the reign title, granted general amnesties, and extended congratulations for longevity—how much more for the vessel transmitting the state?
translations.idiomatic: Since Han and Jin times, whenever precious cauldrons and auspicious objects were obtained, the court still announced them at the ancestral temple, changed the reign title, proclaimed general amnesties, and extended congratulations for longevity—how much more so for the vessel transmitting the state?

sentences.zh: 其緣寶法物禮儀，乞下所屬施行。

translations.literal: We beg that the ritual procedures for the accompanying objects of the treasure be sent down to the responsible offices for implementation.
translations.idiomatic: We respectfully request that the ritual procedures governing the treasure's accompanying objects be transmitted to the responsible offices for implementation.

sentences.zh: 詔禮部、太常寺按故事詳定以聞。

translations.literal: An edict ordered the Ministry of Rites and the Court of Imperial Sacrifices to examine precedents in detail and report.
translations.idiomatic: An edict directed the Ministry of Rites and the Court of Imperial Sacrifices to examine precedents in detail and report their findings.

sentences.zh: 禮官言：五月朔，故事當大朝會，宜就行受寶之禮。

translations.literal: The ritual officials stated: On the first day of the fifth month, according to precedent there should be a great court assembly; the ceremony of receiving the treasure should be carried out on that occasion.
translations.idiomatic: The ritual officials reported: On the first day of the fifth month, by established precedent a great court assembly was scheduled; the ceremony of receiving the treasure should be conducted on that day.

sentences.zh: 依上尊號寶冊儀，有司豫製緣寶法物，並寶進入。

translations.literal: Following the protocol for honorific titles, treasures, and volumes, the responsible offices shall prepare in advance the ritual objects accompanying the treasure, and the treasure shall be brought in.
translations.idiomatic: Following the protocol for honorific titles, treasures, and volumes, the responsible offices were to prepare the ritual paraphernalia accompanying the treasure in advance and present the treasure.

sentences.zh: 俟降出，權於寶堂安奉。

translations.literal: When it is brought down and presented, it shall temporarily be installed for veneration in the Treasure Hall.
translations.idiomatic: Once presented, it was to be temporarily installed for veneration in the Treasure Hall.

sentences.zh: 前三日，差官奏告天地、宗廟、社稷。

translations.literal: Three days beforehand, officers shall be dispatched to announce it to Heaven and Earth, the ancestral temple, and the altars of soil and grain.
translations.idiomatic: Three days in advance, officers were to announce the event to Heaven and Earth, the ancestral temple, and the altars of soil and grain.

sentences.zh: 前一日，帝齋於內殿。

translations.literal: On the preceding day, the emperor shall fast in the inner hall.
translations.idiomatic: On the day before, the emperor was to observe a fast in the inner hall.

sentences.zh: 翌日，禦大慶殿，降坐受寶，群臣上壽稱賀。

translations.literal: On the following day, he shall preside in the Hall of Great Celebration, descend from the throne to receive the treasure, and the hundred officials shall offer congratulations for longevity.
translations.idiomatic: On the appointed day, he was to preside in the Hall of Great Celebration, descend from the throne to receive the treasure, and the officials were to offer congratulations for longevity.

sentences.zh: 先期，又詔龍圖、天章閣齎治平元年耀州所獻受命寶玉檢，赴都堂參議。

translations.literal: In advance, an edict also ordered the Dragon Diagram and Heavenly Writ archives to bring the jade tablet of the treasure of received mandate presented by Yaozhou in the first year of Zhiping for joint deliberation at the chief ministers' hall.
translations.idiomatic: In advance, an edict also ordered the Dragon Diagram and Heavenly Writ archives to bring the jade tablet of the treasure of received mandate presented by Yaozhou in the first year of Zhiping to the chief ministers' hall for joint deliberation.

sentences.zh: 詔以五月朔受傳國寶，命章惇書玉檢，以「天授傳國受命之寶」為文。

translations.literal: An edict ordered that on the first day of the fifth month the seal transmitting the state be received, and Zhang Dun was commanded to inscribe the jade tablet with the text "Treasure of Heaven's Grant Transmitting the State and Received Mandate."
translations.idiomatic: An edict directed that on the first day of the fifth month the seal transmitting the state be received, and Zhang Dun was commanded to inscribe the jade tablet with the text "Treasure of Heaven's Grant Transmitting the State and Received Mandate."

sentences.zh: 徽宗崇寧五年，有以玉印獻者。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Chongning under Huizong, someone presented a jade seal.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of the Chongning reign under Emperor Huizong, someone presented a jade seal.

sentences.zh: 印方寸，以龜為鈕，工作精巧，文曰「承天福延萬億永無極」。

translations.literal: The seal was one cun square, with a turtle knob; the workmanship was exquisitely refined, and the inscription read "Receiving Heaven's blessing, extending myriadss, eternally without limit."
translations.idiomatic: The seal was one inch square, with a turtle knob; its craftsmanship was exquisitely refined, and its inscription read "Receiving Heaven's blessing, extending myriadss, eternally without limit."

sentences.zh: 徽宗因次其文，仿李斯蟲魚篆作寶文。

translations.literal: Huizong thereupon extended its text and, imitating Li Si's insect-and-fish seal script, composed the treasure inscription.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Huizong then elaborated its text and, imitating Li Si's insect-and-fish seal script, composed the inscription for a new treasure.

sentences.zh: 其方四寸有奇，螭鈕，方盤，上圓下方，名為鎮國寶。

translations.literal: It was four odd cun square, with a chi knob, a square base, round above and square below, and was named the Treasure for Stabilizing the State.
translations.idiomatic: The treasure was somewhat more than four inches square, with a chi knob, a square base, round above and square below, and was named the Treasure for Stabilizing the State.

sentences.zh: 大觀元年，又得玉工，用元豐中玉琢天子、皇帝六璽，疊篆。

translations.literal: In the first year of Daguan, jade craftsmen were again obtained; using jade from the Yuanfeng period they carved the Son of Heaven's and emperor's six seals in stacked seal script.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Daguan, skilled jade craftsmen were again secured; using jade stock from the Yuanfeng period they carved the Son of Heaven's and emperor's six seals in stacked seal script.

sentences.zh: 初，紹聖間，得漢傳國璽，無檢，螭又不闕，疑其一角缺者，乃檢也。

translations.literal: Initially, during the Shaosheng period, the Han seal for transmitting the state was obtained, without a tablet; the chi was also not broken off; it was suspected that what was missing at one corner was the tablet.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, during the Shaosheng reign, the Han seal for transmitting the state had been obtained without its tablet; the chi knob was also intact; it was suspected that the missing corner piece was the tablet.

sentences.zh: 有《檢傳》，考驗甚詳，傳於世。

translations.literal: There is a "Transmission of the Tablet," with very detailed verification, transmitted in the world.
translations.idiomatic: A document titled "Transmission of the Tablet" circulated in the world, offering very detailed authentication.

sentences.zh: 帝於是取其文而黜其璽不用，自作受命寶，其方四寸有奇，琢以白玉，篆以蟲魚。

translations.literal: The emperor therefore took its inscription and rejected the seal itself, not using it; he made a treasure of received mandate himself, somewhat more than four cun square, carved from white jade, inscribed in insect-and-fish script.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor therefore adopted its inscription but set the seal itself aside; he personally commissioned a treasure of received mandate, somewhat more than four inches square, carved from white jade and inscribed in insect-and-fish script.

sentences.zh: 鎮國、受命二寶，合天子、皇帝六璽，是為八寶。

translations.literal: The treasures for stabilizing the state and received mandate, together with the Son of Heaven's and emperor's six seals, made eight treasures in all.
translations.idiomatic: The treasures for stabilizing the state and received mandate, together with the Son of Heaven's and emperor's six seals, constituted eight treasures in all.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「自昔皆有尚符璽官。

translations.literal: An edict stated: "From antiquity there have always been officials in charge of seals and credentials.
translations.idiomatic: An edict declared: "From antiquity there have always been officials charged with guarding seals and credentials.

sentences.zh: 今雖隸門下後省，遇親祠，則臨時具員，訖事復罷。

translations.literal: Today, although subordinate to the Rear Secretariat under the Gate, when there are personal sacrifices they temporarily fill the posts and, when the affair is concluded, are again dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Although they now fall under the Rear Secretariat of the Gate Department, for personal sacrifices they are temporarily appointed and dismissed once the rite concludes.

sentences.zh: 八寶既備，宜重典司之職。

translations.literal: Now that the eight treasures are complete, the office charged with them should be given weight.
translations.idiomatic: Now that the eight treasures are complete, the office overseeing them should be restored to proper importance.

sentences.zh: 可令尚書省置官，如古之制。」

translations.literal: The Ministry of Personnel may establish officials as in antiquity."
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of Personnel should establish dedicated officials as in antiquity.

sentences.zh: 又詔曰：「永惟受命之符，當有一代之制，而尚循秦舊，六璽之用，度越百年之久，或未大備。

translations.literal: Another edict stated: "Ever considering the credential of received mandate, there ought to be an institution for each generation; yet we still follow the Qin old system of six seals—over more than a century the usage may not have been fully complete.
translations.idiomatic: A further edict stated: "Ever mindful that the credential of received mandate should have an institution proper to each generation, we have nevertheless continued the Qin-era system of six seals—for more than a century the usage may not have been fully complete.

sentences.zh: 自天申命，地不愛寶，獲全玉於異域，得妙工於編氓，八寶既成，敻無前比，殆天所授，非人能為。

translations.literal: Since Heaven bestowed the mandate and the earth did not begrudge its treasures, whole jade was obtained from foreign lands and master craftsmen from among the common people; once the eight treasures were completed, they were without precedent in remotest antiquity—likely a gift from Heaven, not something human hands could achieve.
translations.idiomatic: Once Heaven renewed the mandate and the earth withheld no treasure, whole jade was obtained from distant lands and master craftsmen from among the people; when the eight treasures were finished, they had no precedent even in high antiquity—surely a gift from Heaven, not the work of human hands alone.

sentences.zh: 可以來年元日，禦大慶殿恭受八寶。」

translations.literal: On New Year's Day of the coming year, the emperor may preside in the Hall of Great Celebration and reverently receive the eight treasures."
translations.idiomatic: On New Year's Day of the coming year, the emperor may preside in the Hall of Great Celebration and reverently receive the eight treasures.

sentences.zh: 尚書省言：

translations.literal: The Ministry of Personnel stated:
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of Personnel reported:

sentences.zh: 請置符寶郎四員，隸門下省，二員以中人充，掌寶於禁中。

translations.literal: We request that four seal-and-credential officers be established, subordinate to the Secretariat under the Gate; two posts to be filled by eunuchs, who shall keep the treasures within the inner palace.
translations.idiomatic: We request that four seal-and-credential officers be established under the Secretariat of the Gate Department, two of the posts to be filled by eunuchs charged with keeping the treasures within the inner palace.

sentences.zh: 按唐八寶，車駕臨幸，則符寶郎奉寶以從；

translations.literal: According to the Tang eight treasures, when the imperial carriage went on tour, the seal-and-credential officer bore the treasures to follow;
translations.idiomatic: Under the Tang system of eight treasures, when the imperial carriage went on tour, the seal-and-credential officer bore the treasures in attendance;

sentences.zh: 大朝會，則奉寶以進。

translations.literal: at great court assemblies, he presented the treasures.
translations.idiomatic: at great court assemblies, he presented the treasures.

sentences.zh: 今鎮國寶、受命寶非常用之器，欲臨幸則從六寶，朝會則陳八寶，皆夕納。

translations.literal: Today the treasures for stabilizing the state and received mandate are not objects of daily use; on imperial tours the six treasures alone should follow; at court assemblies all eight should be displayed—each to be stored away in the evening.
translations.idiomatic: Today the treasures for stabilizing the state and received mandate are not suited for daily use; on imperial tours only the six treasures should accompany the emperor; at court assemblies all eight should be displayed—each to be secured away each evening.

sentences.zh: 內符寶郎奉寶出以授外符寶郎，外符寶郎從寶行於禁衛之內，朝則分進於御坐之前。

translations.literal: The inner seal-and-credential officer brings the treasure out and hands it to the outer seal-and-credential officer; the outer officer carries the treasure within the inner guard, and at court they are separately presented before the imperial seat.
translations.idiomatic: The inner seal-and-credential officer brings the treasure forth and hands it to the outer officer, who carries it within the inner guard; at court they are presented separately before the imperial seat.

sentences.zh: 鎮國寶、受命寶不常用，唯封禪則用之。

translations.literal: The treasures for stabilizing the state and received mandate are not commonly used; only for Fengshan are they employed.
translations.idiomatic: The treasures for stabilizing the state and received mandate are not in common use; they are employed only for Fengshan.

sentences.zh: 皇帝之寶，答鄰國書則用之；

translations.literal: The emperor's treasure is used when replying to neighboring states' documents;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's treasure is used when replying to documents from neighboring states;

sentences.zh: 皇帝行寶，降御劄則用之；

translations.literal: the emperor's traveling treasure when issuing imperial rescripts;
translations.idiomatic: the emperor's traveling treasure when issuing imperial rescripts;

sentences.zh: 皇帝信寶，賜鄰國書及物則用之；

translations.literal: the emperor's credential treasure when bestowing documents and goods on neighboring states;
translations.idiomatic: the emperor's credential treasure when bestowing documents and goods upon neighboring states;

sentences.zh: 天子之寶，答外國書則用之；

translations.literal: the Son of Heaven's treasure when replying to foreign states' documents;
translations.idiomatic: the Son of Heaven's treasure when replying to documents from foreign states;

sentences.zh: 天子行寶，封冊則用之；

translations.literal: the Son of Heaven's traveling treasure when issuing investiture documents;
translations.idiomatic: the Son of Heaven's traveling treasure when issuing investiture documents;

sentences.zh: 天子信寶，舉大兵則用之。

translations.literal: the Son of Heaven's credential treasure when mobilizing great armies.
translations.idiomatic: the Son of Heaven's credential treasure when mobilizing great armies.

sentences.zh: 應合用寶，外符寶郎具奏，請內符寶郎御前請寶，印訖，付外符寶郎承受。

translations.literal: Whenever a treasure is required, the outer seal-and-credential officer shall memorialize; the inner officer shall request the treasure before the emperor, and after impressing it shall hand it to the outer officer to receive.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever a treasure was required, the outer seal-and-credential officer was to memorialize; the inner officer was to request the treasure before the emperor, and after impressing the document was to hand it to the outer officer for delivery.

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: The request was approved.
translations.idiomatic: The court approved the proposal.

sentences.zh: 二年，詔受命寶之上，加「鎮國」二字。

translations.literal: In the second year, an edict ordered that above the treasure of received mandate the two characters "Stabilizing the State" be added.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year, an edict directed that the two characters "Stabilizing the State" be added above the treasure of received mandate.

sentences.zh: 政和七年，從于闐得大玉逾二尺，色如截肪。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Zhenghe, from Khotan a great jade was obtained exceeding two chi, its color like a severed fat-streak.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year of Zhenghe, from Khotan a great jade was obtained exceeding two feet in length, its color like freshly cut fat.

sentences.zh: 徽宗又製一寶，赤螭鈕，文曰「範圍天地，幽讚神明，保合太和，萬壽無疆」。

translations.literal: Huizong also made a treasure, with a red chi knob, inscribed "Encompassing heaven and earth, silently assisting the spirits, preserving the great harmony, myriad years without bound."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Huizong also commissioned a treasure with a red chi knob, inscribed "Encompassing heaven and earth, silently assisting the spirits, preserving the great harmony, myriad years without bound."

sentences.zh: 篆以魚蟲，製作之工，幾於秦璽。

translations.literal: Inscribed in fish-and-insect script, the workmanship nearly matched the Qin seal.
translations.idiomatic: Inscribed in fish-and-insect script, its craftsmanship nearly rivaled the Qin seal.

sentences.zh: 其寶九寸，檢亦如之，號曰「定命寶」。

translations.literal: The treasure was nine cun, and the tablet likewise; it was titled the "Treasure for Fixing Destiny."
translations.idiomatic: The treasure measured nine inches, and its tablet likewise; it was titled the "Treasure for Fixing Destiny."

sentences.zh: 合前八寶為九，詔以九寶為稱，以定命寶為首。

translations.literal: Together with the previous eight treasures they made nine; an edict ordered that the nine treasures be the designation, with the treasure for fixing destiny as foremost.
translations.idiomatic: Together with the previous eight treasures they made nine; an edict declared that the nine treasures should be the formal designation, with the treasure for fixing destiny placed foremost.

sentences.zh: 且曰：「八寶者，國之神器；

translations.literal: Moreover it said: "The Eight Treasures are the sacred vessels of the state;
translations.idiomatic: It was further declared: "The Eight Treasures constitute the supreme regalia of the realm;

sentences.zh: 至於定命寶，乃我所自製也。」

translations.literal: As for the Treasure of Fixing Fate, it is one that I made myself."
translations.idiomatic: The Treasure of Fixing Fate, however, was fashioned by my own hand."

sentences.zh: 於是，應行導排設，定命與受命、天子寶在左，鎮國與皇帝寶在右。

translations.literal: Therefore, according to the prescribed procession arrangement, the Treasures of Fixing Fate, Received Mandate, and Son of Heaven were placed on the left, and the Treasures of Stabilizing the Realm and Emperor were placed on the right.
translations.idiomatic: Accordingly, in the ceremonial order of march, Fixing Fate stood with Received Mandate and the Son of Heaven treasures on the left, while Stabilizing the Realm and the Emperor treasures took the right.

sentences.zh: 又詔：「鎮國、受命寶與天子、皇帝之寶，其數有八，蓋非乾元用九之數。

translations.literal: Another edict stated: "The Treasures of Stabilizing the Realm, Received Mandate, and those of Son of Heaven and Emperor number eight in all—this is decidedly not the number nine used in the Qian primordial hexagram.
translations.idiomatic: A further decree explained: "Stabilizing the Realm, Received Mandate, and the Son of Heaven and Emperor seals together make eight—not the nine of the Qian hexagram's creative fullness.

sentences.zh: 比得寶玉於異哉，受定命之符於神霄，乃以『範圍天地，幽讚神明，保合太和，萬壽無疆』為文。

translations.literal: Having recently obtained precious jade from foreign lands and received the talisman of fixing fate at the Divine Empyrean, the inscription was set as "Encompassing Heaven and Earth, praising the spirits in the hidden realm, preserving and harmonizing the Great Harmony, boundless longevity."
translations.idiomatic: After jade of rare quality was acquired from abroad and the Fixing Fate token received at the Divine Empyrean, the text chosen was: "Spanning Heaven and Earth, honoring the hidden gods, sustaining perfect harmony, longevity without limit."

sentences.zh: 卜雲其吉，篆以蟲魚，縱廣之制，其寸亦九，號曰定命寶。

translations.literal: A divination showed auspicious clouds; it was inscribed in seal script in the style of worms and fish; its length and width measured nine inches each; it was named the Treasure of Fixing Fate.
translations.idiomatic: Divination revealed favorable clouds, and the seal was cut in ancient worm-and-fish script; its dimensions were nine inches on every side, and it was called the Treasure of Fixing Fate.

sentences.zh: 來年元日祗受。」

translations.literal: It shall be reverently received on New Year's Day of the coming year."
translations.idiomatic: The formal investiture was set for the first day of the new year.

sentences.zh: 又詔差官奏告天地、宗廟、祖稷。

translations.literal: Another edict ordered officials to be dispatched to report to Heaven and Earth, the ancestral temples, and the altars of grain and soil.
translations.idiomatic: Officials were also appointed to announce the event before Heaven and Earth, the imperial temples, and the altars of the land.

sentences.zh: 八年正月一日，禦大慶殿，受定命寶，百僚稱賀。

translations.literal: On the first day of the first month of the eighth year, the emperor proceeded to the Hall of Great Celebration to receive the Treasure of Fixing Fate, and all officials offered congratulations.
translations.idiomatic: On New Year's Day of the eighth year, the emperor entered the Hall of Great Celebration to receive the Fixing Fate seal, and the entire court offered felicitations.

sentences.zh: 其後京城之難，諸寶俱失之，惟大宋受命之寶與定命寶獨存，蓋天意也。

translations.literal: Afterward, during the disaster in the capital, all the treasures were lost; only the Treasure of Received Mandate of Great Song and the Treasure of Fixing Fate survived—surely this was Heaven's intent.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when catastrophe struck the capital, nearly every seal was lost—yet the Great Song Received Mandate seal and the Fixing Fate seal alone remained, which was taken as a sign of Heaven's will.

sentences.zh: 建炎初，始作金寶三：一曰「皇帝欽崇國祀之寶」，祭祀祠表用之；

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Jianyan era, three gold treasures were first made: the first called "Treasure of the Emperor Reverently Honoring State Sacrifices," used for sacrificial rites and memorial petitions to the temples;
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Jianyan reign, three new gold seals were cast: the first, "Treasure of the Emperor's Reverent State Sacrifice," reserved for temple offerings and sacrificial memorials;

sentences.zh: 二曰「天下合同之寶」，降付中書門下省用之；

translations.literal: The second called "Treasure of All Under Heaven in Unity," delivered to the Secretariat-Chancellery for use;
translations.idiomatic: The second, "Treasure of Universal Accord," entrusted to the Secretariat-Chancellery;

sentences.zh: 三曰「書詔之寶」，發號施令用之。

translations.literal: The third called "Treasure for Writing Edicts," used for issuing commands and decrees.
translations.idiomatic: The third, "Treasure for Written Edicts," employed whenever the throne issued orders and proclamations.

sentences.zh: 紹興元年，又作玉寶一，文曰「大宋受命中興之寶」。

translations.literal: In the first year of the Shaoxing era, another jade treasure was made, inscribed "Treasure of Great Song's Received Mandate and Restoration."
translations.idiomatic: In Shaoxing 1, a jade seal was added bearing the legend "Treasure of Great Song's Mandate and Restoration."

sentences.zh: 又得舊寶二，曆世寶之，凡上太上皇尊號、冊後太子皆用焉。

translations.literal: Two old treasures were also recovered, treasured through successive reigns; they were used whenever bestowing honorific titles upon the Retired Emperor and investiture of the crown prince's consort.
translations.idiomatic: Two earlier seals were also recovered and preserved through the ages; these served whenever a retired emperor received a new honorific or a crown prince's consort was invested.

sentences.zh: 十六年，又作八寶：一曰護國神寶，以「承天福延萬億永無極」九字為文；

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year, eight treasures were again made: the first, the Divine Treasure for Protecting the State, with the nine-character inscription "Receiving Heaven's blessing, extending ten thousand millions, eternally without limit";
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year, the full set of eight seals was renewed: first, the Divine Treasure for Protecting the State, inscribed with nine characters reading "Heaven's favor received, myriads prolonged, forever without end";

sentences.zh: 二曰受命寶，以「受命於天既壽永昌」為文；

translations.literal: The second, the Treasure of Received Mandate, with the inscription "Having received the mandate from Heaven, long life and eternal prosperity";
translations.idiomatic: Second, the Received Mandate seal, bearing the classic phrase "Mandate received from Heaven—long life and lasting glory";

sentences.zh: 三曰天子之寶；

translations.literal: The third, the Treasure of the Son of Heaven;
translations.idiomatic: Third, the Son of Heaven seal;

sentences.zh: 四曰天子信寶；

translations.literal: The fourth, the Credential Treasure of the Son of Heaven;
translations.idiomatic: Fourth, the Son of Heaven credential seal;

sentences.zh: 五曰天子行寶；

translations.literal: The fifth, the Traveling Treasure of the Son of Heaven;
translations.idiomatic: Fifth, the Son of Heaven traveling seal;

sentences.zh: 六曰皇帝之寶；

translations.literal: The sixth, the Treasure of the Emperor;
translations.idiomatic: Sixth, the Emperor seal;

sentences.zh: 七曰皇帝信寶；

translations.literal: The seventh, the Credential Treasure of the Emperor;
translations.idiomatic: Seventh, the Emperor credential seal;

sentences.zh: 八曰皇帝行寶。

translations.literal: The eighth, the Traveling Treasure of the Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Eighth, the Emperor traveling seal.

sentences.zh: 藏之禦府，大朝會則陳之；

translations.literal: They were stored in the Imperial Treasury and displayed at grand court assemblies;
translations.idiomatic: These were kept in the imperial vault and brought out for major court audiences;

sentences.zh: 上冊寶尊號、冊後太子、大禮設鹵簿，亦如之。

translations.literal: When conferring seal-treasures and honorific titles, investituting the crown prince's consort, or arranging the full guard of honor for major ceremonies, they were likewise brought forth.
translations.idiomatic: The same practice applied when bestowing honorific seals upon a retired emperor, investing an empress or crown prince's consort, or mounting the full ceremonial guard for state rites.

sentences.zh: 寶之制，用玉尺度，鈕鼻，大小綬，玉環。

translations.literal: The specifications for the treasures: measured by the jade standard ruler, with a knob and loop, large and small cords, and jade rings.
translations.idiomatic: Each seal was sized by the jade measure, fitted with a knob and loop, hung with great and lesser cords, and linked with jade rings.

sentences.zh: 檢製，舊制如牌，上刻曰某寶。

translations.literal: Inspection tags were made according to the old system like plaques, engraved atop with the name of the given treasure.
translations.idiomatic: Verification plaques followed the older design: flat tags inscribed on top with the seal's name.

sentences.zh: 皆裹以朱縷，加緋羅泥金帕，納於小盝。

translations.literal: All were wrapped in vermilion cord, covered with crimson silk gold-paste cloth, and placed in small cases.
translations.idiomatic: Each was bound in red thread, wrapped in crimson silk overlaid with gold paste, and enclosed in a small box.

sentences.zh: 盝三重，皆飾以金，內設金床、金寶鬥，龍鑰金鎖，覆以緋羅繡帕，載以腰輿、行馬。

translations.literal: The cases were triple-layered, all trimmed with gold; inside were set a gold bed and gold treasure socket; dragon keys and gold locks secured them; they were covered with embroidered crimson silk cloth, and carried on waist-litters and travel mounts.
translations.idiomatic: Three nested cases, all gold-trimmed, held a gold cradle and gold seal socket within; dragon-shaped keys and gold locks fastened them, brocaded crimson silk covered them, and they were borne on sedan chairs and carrying frames.

sentences.zh: 孝宗即位，議上太上皇帝尊號曰光堯壽聖太上皇帝，寶用皇祐中法、黍尺量度。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaozong acceded, it was proposed to bestow the honorific title Grand Retired Emperor Guangyao Shousheng upon the Retired Emperor; the treasure was measured according to the Huangyou standard and the millet measure.
translations.idiomatic: Upon Xiaozong's accession, officials proposed the honorific Guangyao Shousheng Grand Retired Emperor for his predecessor, and the seal was dimensioned by the Huangyou court measure and the millet foot-rule.

sentences.zh: 乾道六年，再加十四字尊號，以寶材元係螭龍鈕，止堪改作蹲龍，其鈕高二寸四分五厘，厚一寸一分五厘，竅徑一寸。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Qiandao, a further fourteen-character honorific title was added; since the treasure material originally bore a hornless dragon knob, it could only be remade as a crouching dragon; the knob was two inches, four fen, five li in height, one inch, one fen, five li thick, with an aperture one inch in diameter.
translations.idiomatic: In Qiandao 6, fourteen more characters were added to the honorific; because the original stone bore a hornless-dragon knob, it could be recut only as a crouching dragon—two inches four fen five li tall, one inch one fen five li thick, with a one-inch bore.

sentences.zh: 理宗寶慶三年，加上寧宗皇帝徽號，寶麵廣四寸二分，厚一寸二分，蹲龍鈕，通高四寸一分，寶四面鉤碾行龍。

translations.literal: In the third year of Baqing under Emperor Lizong, the posthumous honorific title was added for Emperor Ningzong; the face of the treasure was four inches, two fen wide, one inch, two fen thick, with a crouching dragon knob, total height four inches, one fen, with roaming dragons carved in relief on all four sides of the treasure.
translations.idiomatic: In Baqing 3, Lizong added Ningzong's posthumous honorific seal: the face four inches two fen across, one inch two fen thick, crouching-dragon knob, four inches one fen overall, with striding dragons chased in relief on all four faces.

sentences.zh: 后妃之寶。

translations.literal: The treasures of empresses and consorts.
translations.idiomatic: Seals of empresses and imperial consorts.

sentences.zh: 哲宗元祐元年，詔：天聖中，章獻明肅皇后用玉寶，方四寸九分，厚一寸二分，龍鈕。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yuanyou under Emperor Zhezong, an edict stated: During the Tiansheng era, Empress Zhangxian Mingsu used a jade treasure, square, four inches, nine fen on a side, one inch, two fen thick, with a dragon knob.
translations.idiomatic: In Yuanyou 1, Zhezong decreed: Under Tiansheng, Empress Zhangxian Mingsu had employed a jade seal four inches nine fen square, one inch two fen thick, with a dragon knob.

sentences.zh: 今太皇太后權同處分軍國事，宜依章獻明肅皇后故事。

translations.literal: Now that the Grand Empress Dowager provisionally shares in the disposition of state and military affairs, she should follow the precedent of Empress Zhangxian Mingsu.
translations.idiomatic: Since the Grand Empress Dowager now held provisional authority over state and military affairs, she was to follow Zhangxian Mingsu's precedent.

sentences.zh: 二年，又詔：太皇太后玉寶，以「太皇太后之寶」為文；

translations.literal: In the second year, another edict stated: The Grand Empress Dowager's jade treasure bore the inscription "Treasure of the Grand Empress Dowager";
translations.idiomatic: The following year, a decree specified: the Grand Empress Dowager's jade seal was inscribed "Treasure of the Grand Empress Dowager";

sentences.zh: 皇太后金寶，以「皇太后寶」為文；

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager's gold treasure bore the inscription "Treasure of the Empress Dowager";
translations.idiomatic: The Empress Dowager's gold seal read "Treasure of the Empress Dowager";

sentences.zh: 皇太妃金寶，以「皇太妃寶」為文。

translations.literal: The Imperial Consort's gold treasure bore the inscription "Treasure of the Imperial Consort."
translations.idiomatic: The Imperial Consort's gold seal read "Treasure of the Imperial Consort."

sentences.zh: 中興之後，後寶用金，方二寸四分，高下隨宜，鼻紐以龜。

translations.literal: After the Restoration, the consorts' treasures were made of gold, square, two inches, four fen on a side, with height adjusted as appropriate, with turtle-shaped knobs and loops.
translations.idiomatic: Following the Restoration, empresses' seals were cast in gold, two inches four fen square, proportioned as needed, with turtle-form knobs.

sentences.zh: 鬥、檢以銀，塗以金。

translations.literal: The sockets and inspection tags were of silver, gilded.
translations.idiomatic: Seal sockets and verification plaques were silver, then gilt.

sentences.zh: 寶盝三重，鈒百花，塗金盤鳳。

translations.literal: The treasure cases were triple-layered, embossed with a hundred flowers, gilded with coiling phoenixes.
translations.idiomatic: Cases came in three nested layers, chased with floral designs and gilded with coiled phoenixes.

sentences.zh: 輿案、行馬、帕褥亦如之。

translations.literal: The litter tables, travel mounts, and cloth padding were likewise appointed.
translations.idiomatic: Carrying frames, sedan mounts, and silk wrappings matched the same standard.

sentences.zh: 皇太子寶。

translations.literal: The crown prince's treasure.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince's seal.

sentences.zh: 至道元年，製皇太子受冊金寶。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhidao, the gold investiture treasure for the crown prince was made.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhidao 1, a gold seal was fashioned for the crown prince's investiture.

sentences.zh: 方二寸，厚五寸，係以朱組大綬，連玉環，金鬥。

translations.literal: It was two inches square, five inches thick, attached with a great vermilion cord, linked to jade rings and a gold socket.
translations.idiomatic: Two inches on each face and five inches thick, it was hung with a great red cord, jade rings, and a gold seal socket.

sentences.zh: 金檢長五寸，闊二寸，厚二分。

translations.literal: The gold inspection tag was five inches long, two inches wide, and two fen thick.
translations.idiomatic: Its gold verification plaque measured five inches by two inches and two fen thick.

sentences.zh: 裹以紅綿。

translations.literal: It was wrapped in red cotton.
translations.idiomatic: Red cotton padding wrapped the seal.

sentences.zh: 加紅羅泥金巴，納於小盝。

translations.literal: Covered with red silk gold-paste cloth, it was placed in a small case.
translations.idiomatic: A red silk cover with gold paste enclosed it in a small box.

sentences.zh: 盝以金裝，內設金床。

translations.literal: The case was trimmed with gold, with a gold bed set inside.
translations.idiomatic: The box was gold-mounted and lined with a gold cradle within.

sentences.zh: 又盝二重，皆覆以紅羅銷金巴。

translations.literal: Two more case layers were added, all covered with red silk cut-gold cloth.
translations.idiomatic: Two outer cases followed, each draped in red silk with cut-gold ornament.

sentences.zh: 盝及腰輿、行馬皆銀裝金塗。

translations.literal: The cases, waist-litters, and travel mounts were all silver-mounted and gilded.
translations.idiomatic: Cases, carrying chairs, and transport frames were silver-fitted and gilt.

sentences.zh: 他法物皆銀為之，鈒花塗金。

translations.literal: Other ritual objects were all made of silver, embossed with flowers and gilded.
translations.idiomatic: All accompanying ritual gear was silver, floral-chased, and gilded.

sentences.zh: 中興，寶，龜鈕；

translations.literal: After the Restoration, the treasure had a turtle knob;
translations.idiomatic: Under the restored dynasty, the seal bore a turtle-form knob;

sentences.zh: 金塗銀檢，上勒「皇太子寶」四字，金塗銀寶鬥。

translations.literal: Gilded silver inspection tags bore the four characters "Treasure of the Crown Prince" engraved upon them, with gilded silver treasure sockets.
translations.idiomatic: Gilt silver plaques were engraved "Treasure of the Crown Prince," with matching gilt silver seal sockets.

sentences.zh: 黝漆盝三重，並錦拓裏，外以金塗銀百花鳳葉子五明裝，鑰以金鎖，載以黝漆腰輿、行馬。

translations.literal: Triple black-lacquered cases, all lined with brocade, externally adorned with gilded silver five-bright ornamentation of hundred-flower phoenix leaves, secured with gold locks, carried on black-lacquered waist-litters and travel mounts.
translations.idiomatic: Three black-lacquer cases, brocade-lined, were clad outside in gilt silver phoenix-and-flower openwork, locked with gold, and borne on black-lacquer sedan chairs and carrying frames.

sentences.zh: 冊製。

translations.literal: Specifications for investiture registers.
translations.idiomatic: Regulations governing investiture scrolls.

sentences.zh: 用瑉玉，簡長一尺二寸，闊一寸二分；

translations.literal: Made of min jade, each tablet one foot, two inches long and one inch, two fen wide;
translations.idiomatic: They were cut from min jade into slips one foot two inches long and one inch two fen wide;

sentences.zh: 簡數從字之多少。

translations.literal: The number of tablets depended on the length of the text.
translations.idiomatic: The count of slips varied with the length of the inscription.

sentences.zh: 聯以金繩，首尾結帶。

translations.literal: Linked with gold cord, tied at both ends into bands.
translations.idiomatic: Gold cord bound them together, knotted at either end.

sentences.zh: 前後褾首四枚，二枚畫神，二枚刻龍鏤金，若奉護之狀。

translations.literal: At front and rear were four cover plates: two painted with spirits, two carved with dragons and gilded, as if in the manner of offering protection.
translations.idiomatic: Four end-caps front and back—two painted with divine figures, two dragon-carved and gilt—presented the aspect of guardians bearing the text.

sentences.zh: 藉以錦褥，覆以緋羅泥金夾帕。

translations.literal: Laid upon brocade cushions, covered with crimson silk gold-paste double cloth.
translations.idiomatic: They rested on brocade mats beneath a double layer of crimson silk with gold paste.

sentences.zh: 冊匣長廣取容冊，塗以朱漆，金鏤百花凸起行龍，金鎖、分錔。

translations.literal: The register case was sized to hold the register, coated with cinnabar lacquer, with gold openwork of a hundred flowers and raised roaming dragons, gold locks and clasps.
translations.idiomatic: The scroll casket was sized to fit the text, lacquered red, decorated with gilt openwork flowers and raised striding dragons, and fitted with gold locks and clasps.

sentences.zh: 覆以紅羅繡盤龍蹙金巴，承以金裝長竿床，金龍首，金魚鉤，又以紅絲為絛縈匣。

translations.literal: Covered with red silk embroidered coiling dragon gold-embroidered cloth, supported on a gold-trimmed long-pole stand with a gold dragon head and gold fish hook, and bound with red silk cords around the case.
translations.idiomatic: A red silk cover embroidered with coiled dragons in gold thread draped it; a gold-mounted long pole with dragon head and fish hook bore the casket, which was further bound with red silk cords.

sentences.zh: 冊案塗朱漆，以銷金紅羅覆之。

translations.literal: The register table was coated with cinnabar lacquer and covered with cut-gold red silk.
translations.idiomatic: The presentation table was lacquered red and draped in red silk with cut-gold work.

sentences.zh: 後冊，用瑉，或以象。

translations.literal: Registers for empresses used min jade, or sometimes ivory.
translations.idiomatic: Empresses' investiture scrolls were of min jade or, alternatively, ivory.

sentences.zh: 縷文以鳳，尺寸制度並同帝冊。

translations.literal: The threaded ornamentation featured phoenixes; dimensions and specifications were the same as the emperor's register.
translations.idiomatic: Phoenix motifs ran through the cordwork, and every dimension matched the emperor's scroll.

sentences.zh: 皇太子冊，用瑉簡六十枚，乾道中，用七十五枚，每枚高尺二寸，博一寸二分。

translations.literal: The crown prince's register used sixty min jade tablets; during Qiandao, seventy-five tablets were used; each tablet was one foot, two inches high and one inch, two fen broad.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince's scroll comprised sixty min jade slips—seventy-five under Qiandao—each one foot two inches tall and one inch two fen wide.

sentences.zh: 前後褾首四枚，長隨簡，博四寸，其二刻神，其二刻龍，為奉護狀。

translations.literal: At front and rear were four cover plates, length matching the tablets, four inches broad; two carved with spirits, two carved with dragons, in the manner of offering protection.
translations.idiomatic: Four end-caps, as long as the slips and four inches wide, flanked the text: two spirit-carved, two dragon-carved, in protective attendance.

sentences.zh: 貫以金絲，首尾結為金花，飾以分錔。

translations.literal: Threaded with gold wire, tied at both ends into gold flowers, adorned with clasps.
translations.idiomatic: Gold filigree threaded the slips, knotted at the ends into floral bosses and finished with segmented clasps.

sentences.zh: 襯以紅羅泥金夾帕，藉以錦褥，盛以黝漆匣，錦拓裏，以金塗銀葉段五明裝，隱起百花鳳。

translations.literal: Lined with red silk gold-paste double cloth, laid upon brocade cushions, stored in a black-lacquered case lined with brocade, with gilded silver leaf-segment five-bright ornamentation, with subtly raised hundred-flower phoenix design.
translations.idiomatic: Red silk with gold paste lined it; brocade cushioned it; a black-lacquer casket with brocade lining and gilt silver openwork in phoenix-and-flower relief held it within.

sentences.zh: 覆以緋羅泥金帕，絡以紅絲結絛，襯以錦褥，載以黝漆腰輿、行馬。

translations.literal: Covered with crimson silk gold-paste cloth, bound with red silk knotted cords, cushioned with brocade, carried on black-lacquered waist-litters and travel mounts.
translations.idiomatic: Crimson silk with gold paste covered it, red cord bound it, brocade padded it, and black-lacquer sedan chairs and frames carried it forth.

sentences.zh: 京湖製置司以所獲亡金寶物來上，令金臣參知政事張天綱辨識。

translations.literal: The Jinghu Pacification Commission presented captured Jin treasures for submission; the Jin subject and Vice Grand Councillor Zhang Tiangang was ordered to identify them.
translations.idiomatic: The Jing-Hu Military Commission forwarded seized Jin regalia to the throne and charged the surrendered Jin minister and Vice Grand Councillor Zhang Tiangang with identifying each piece.

sentences.zh: 其玉寶一，文曰「太祖應乾興運昭德定功睿神莊孝仁明大聖武元皇帝尊諡寶」，乃金人上其祖阿骨打諡寶也。

translations.literal: Among them was one jade treasure, inscribed "Posthumous Honorific Treasure of Emperor Wuyuan, the Great Sage, Martial, Benevolent, Illuminating, Filial, Sagacious, Solemn, Virtuous, Merit-Fixing, Prosperous-Movement, Heaven-Responding Founding Ancestor"—this was the Jin people's posthumous honorific treasure for their ancestor Aguda.
translations.idiomatic: One jade seal read "Posthumous Honorific Seal of Emperor Wuyuan, the Great Sage, Martial, Benevolent, Illuminating, Filial, Sagacious, Solemn, Virtuous, Merit-Fixing, Prosperous-Movement, Heaven-Responding Founding Ancestor"—the Jin dynasty's posthumous seal for their forebear Aguda.

sentences.zh: 其法物有銷金盤龍紅紵絲袍一；

translations.literal: Among the ritual objects was one red kuo-silk robe with cut-gold coiling dragons;
translations.idiomatic: The captured ritual gear included one red kuo-silk robe with cut-gold coiling dragons;

sentences.zh: 透碾雲龍玉帶一，內方八胯結頭一，塌尾一，並玉塗金結頭一，塗金小結攀一；

translations.literal: One jade belt with translucent carved cloud dragons, with one square inner eight-panel knot head, one flat tail, plus one jade gilded knot head and one small gilded knot clasp;
translations.idiomatic: One openwork cloud-dragon jade belt with a square eight-link inner buckle, a flat end piece, a gilt jade buckle head, and a small gilt clasp;

sentences.zh: 連珠環玉束帶一，垂頭裏拓，上有金龍，帶上玉事件大小一十八；

translations.literal: One jade girdle belt with linked pearl rings, with pendant head and lining, bearing a gold dragon atop, with eighteen jade belt ornaments large and small on the belt;
translations.idiomatic: One jade girdle of linked pearl rings, its pendant head lined and crowned with a gold dragon, set with eighteen jade belt fittings of varying size;

sentences.zh: 又玉靶鐵剉一，銷金玉事件二，皮茄袋一，玉事件三。

translations.literal: Also one iron rasp with jade handle, two cut-gold jade belt ornaments, one leather eggplant pouch, and three jade ornaments.
translations.idiomatic: Also a jade-handled iron file, two cut-gold jade fittings, one leather pouch, and three jade ornaments.

sentences.zh: 天綱稱：上項帶，國言謂之「兔鶻」，皆其故主冠顏守緒常服之物也。

translations.literal: Tiangang stated: The belt listed above, called "rabbit-hawk" in the Jin language, were all everyday garments of the former ruler Wanyan Shouxu.
translations.idiomatic: Tiangang testified that the belt above—known in Jin as the "rabbit-hawk"—had belonged to the late emperor Wanyan Shouxu for daily wear.

sentences.zh: 碾玉巾環一，樺皮龍飾角弓一，金龍環刀一，紅紵絲靠枕一，佩玉大環一，皆非臣庶服用之物。

translations.literal: Also one carved jade towel ring, one horn bow decorated with birch bark and dragons, one gold dragon ring-handled knife, one red kuo-silk back cushion, and one large jade ring for wearing—all not objects that subjects and commoners might wear or use.
translations.idiomatic: There were also a carved jade towel ring, a birch-wrapped horn bow with dragon ornament, a gold dragon-hilted ring knife, a red kuo-silk bolster, and a large jade pendant ring—none of them fit for common subjects.

sentences.zh: 製旨冊一本，舊作聖旨，近侍局平日掌此，以承受內降指揮。

translations.literal: One register of Manufactured Edicts—these were formerly called Sacred Edicts, normally kept by the Imperial Attendant Bureau to receive and execute commands issued from within the palace.
translations.idiomatic: One Manufactured Edict register—formerly styled Sacred Edict—was routinely held by the Inner Service Bureau to record commands issued from the palace.

sentences.zh: 壬辰四月，故主援東漢光武故事，令上書者不得言「聖」，故避「聖」字不敢當，因改作「製旨」。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the renchen year, the former ruler cited the precedent of Emperor Guangwu of the Eastern Han, ordering that those submitting memorials must not use the word "sacred"; therefore, avoiding the word "sacred" as unworthy, it was changed to "Manufactured Edict."
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of renchen, the late emperor, invoking Emperor Guangwu of the Eastern Han, forbade memorial writers to use the character for "sacred"; deeming himself unworthy of that term, the title was altered to "Manufactured Edict."

sentences.zh: 外有臣下虎頭金牌三，銀牌八十四，塗金印三，及諸官署銅印三百一十二顆。

translations.literal: Besides these were three tiger-head gold tablets for officials, eighty-four silver tablets, three gilded seals, and three hundred twelve copper seals from various government offices.
translations.idiomatic: In addition there were three tiger-head gold tallies for officials, eighty-four silver tallies, three gilt seals, and three hundred twelve copper office seals.

sentences.zh: 法司以守緒函骨及俘囚故寶、法物等，庭引天綱並護尉都尉完顏好海及天綱妻完顏氏烏古論栲栳、小女瓊瓊一一審實，件列以聞。

translations.literal: The judicial offices, with Wanyan Shouxu's coffined remains and the captured treasures and ritual objects, conducted a court session summoning Tiangang along with Guard Commandant Wanyan Haohai and Tiangang's wife Wanyan Wugulun Kaolao and young daughter Qiongqiong to verify each item one by one, listing them in detail for report.
translations.idiomatic: The judiciary, with Shouxu's coffin and the seized regalia at hand, convened a hearing and summoned Tiangang, Guard Commandant Wanyan Haohai, Tiangang's wife Wugulun Kaolao, and their daughter Qiongqiong to authenticate each article item by item for the court's report.

sentences.zh: 有旨「完顏守緒遺骸並故寶、法物等，藏大理寺獄庫。

translations.literal: An edict stated: "The remains of Wanyan Shouxu together with the former treasures and ritual objects shall be stored in the prison vault of the Court of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: The throne ordered: "Wanyan Shouxu's remains, together with the captured seals and ritual objects, are to be deposited in the vault of the Court of Judicial Review.

sentences.zh: 天綱、好海、完顏氏烏古論、瓊瓊拘諸殿前司，候朝旨」云。

translations.literal: Tiangang, Haohai, Wanyan Wugulun, and Qiongqiong shall be detained by the Palace Bureau, awaiting the court's decree."
translations.idiomatic: Tiangang, Haohai, Wugulun, and Qiongqiong are to be held by the Palace Directorate pending further imperial instruction."

sentences.zh: 印製。

translations.literal: Specifications for seals.
translations.idiomatic: Regulations governing official seals.

sentences.zh: 兩漢以後，人臣有金印、銀印、銅印。

translations.literal: From the Two Han dynasties onward, officials had gold seals, silver seals, and copper seals.
translations.idiomatic: Since the Han dynasties, ministers had been graded with gold, silver, or copper seals.

sentences.zh: 唐制，諸司皆用銅印，宋因之。

translations.literal: Under Tang regulations, all agencies used copper seals; Song followed this practice.
translations.idiomatic: The Tang assigned copper seals to every office, and Song retained the system.

sentences.zh: 諸王及中書門下印方二寸一分，樞密、宣徽、三司、尚書省諸司印方二寸。

translations.literal: Princes and the Secretariat-Chancellery seals were square, two inches, one fen; seals of the Bureau of Military Affairs, Palace Directorate, Commissioner of the Three Departments, and various offices of the Ministry of Personnel were square, two inches.
translations.idiomatic: Princely and Secretariat-Chancellery seals measured two inches one fen square; Military Affairs, Palace Directorate, Three Departments, and Ministry of Personnel office seals were two inches square.

sentences.zh: 惟尚書省印不塗金，餘皆塗金。

translations.literal: Only the Ministry of Personnel seal was not gilded; all others were gilded.
translations.idiomatic: Every seal was gilt except the Ministry of Personnel's own.

sentences.zh: 節度使印方一寸九分，塗金。

translations.literal: Military commissioners' seals were square, one inch, nine fen, gilded.
translations.idiomatic: Circuit military commissioners used gilded seals one inch nine fen square.

sentences.zh: 餘印並方一寸八分，惟觀察使塗金。

translations.literal: All remaining seals were square, one inch, eight fen; only military governors' seals were gilded.
translations.idiomatic: All other seals stood one inch eight fen square; only observation commissioners' seals received gilding.

sentences.zh: 諸王、節度、觀察使、州、府、軍、監、縣印，皆有銅牌，長七寸五分，諸王廣一寸九分，餘廣一寸八分。

translations.literal: Princes, military commissioners, military governors, and prefecture, superior prefecture, army, supervisory, and county seals all had copper plaques, seven inches, five fen long; for princes, one inch, nine fen wide; for others, one inch, eight fen wide.
translations.idiomatic: Princes, circuit commissioners, observation commissioners, and prefectural, army, supervisory, and county offices each kept a copper tally seven inches five fen long—one inch nine fen wide for princes, one inch eight fen for the rest.

sentences.zh: 諸王、節度、觀察使牌塗以金，刻文云「牌出印入，印出牌入」。

translations.literal: Plaques for princes, military commissioners, and military governors were gilded, engraved with the text "When the plaque is out, the seal is in; when the seal is out, the plaque is in."
translations.idiomatic: Princely, circuit, and observation tallies were gilt and inscribed: "Tally out, seal in; seal out, tally in."

sentences.zh: 其奉使出入，或本局無印者，皆給奉使印。

translations.literal: For missions entering and leaving, or where the original office lacked a seal, mission seals were issued.
translations.idiomatic: Envoys on departure or offices without their own seal were furnished with mission seals.

sentences.zh: 景德初，別鑄兩京奉使印。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Jingde era, separate envoy seals for the Two Capitals were cast.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Jingde, distinct envoy seals were cast for the eastern and western capitals.

sentences.zh: 又有朱記，以給京城及外處職司及諸軍將校等，其制長一寸七分，廣一寸六分。

translations.literal: There were also vermilion chops, issued to offices in the capital and outlying regions and to various army officers; they measured one inch, seven fen long and one inch, six fen wide.
translations.idiomatic: Vermilion chops were also issued to capital and provincial offices and to military officers; each measured one inch seven fen by one inch six fen.

sentences.zh: 士庶及寺觀亦有私記。

translations.literal: Commoners and scholar-gentry, as well as temples, also had private chops.
translations.idiomatic: Private seals were permitted to commoners, gentry, and monasteries alike.

sentences.zh: 乾德三年，太祖詔重鑄中書門下、樞密院、三司使印。

translations.literal: In the third year of Qiande, Emperor Taizu ordered the recasting of seals for the Secretariat-Chancellery, Bureau of Military Affairs, and Commissioner of the Three Departments.
translations.idiomatic: In Qiande 3, Taizu commanded new seals for the Secretariat-Chancellery, Military Affairs Bureau, and Three Departments Commission.

sentences.zh: 先是，舊印五代所鑄，篆刻非工。

translations.literal: Previously, the old seals had been cast during the Five Dynasties period, and the seal carving was not finely done.
translations.idiomatic: The seals then in use dated to the Five Dynasties, and their carving had been crude.

sentences.zh: 及得蜀中鑄印官祝溫柔，自言其祖思言，唐禮部鑄印官，世習繆篆，即《漢書·藝文志》所謂「屈曲纏繞，以模印章」者也。

translations.literal: When Zhu Wenrou, the seal-casting officer of Shu, came into their hands, he said himself that his ancestor Siyan had been a Tang Ministry of Rites seal-casting officer, and that the family had practiced twisted seal script for generations—the very script the Book of Han's Treatise on Literature calls 「twisting and coiling to pattern seal impressions.」
translations.idiomatic: Once they secured Zhu Wenrou, the Shu dynasty's master seal caster, he explained that his forebear Siyan had held the same post under the Tang Ministry of Rites, and that his clan had handed down twisted seal script for generations—the ornate, coiling script described in the Book of Han as made for molding seal impressions.

sentences.zh: 思言隨僖宗入蜀，子孫遂為蜀人。

translations.literal: Siyan followed Emperor Xizong into Shu, and his descendants thus became people of Shu.
translations.idiomatic: Siyan followed Emperor Xizong when the court fled into Shu, and his descendants remained there as Sichuan natives.

sentences.zh: 自是，台、省、寺、監及開封府、興元尹印，悉令溫柔重改鑄焉。

translations.literal: From this time, the seals of the departments, ministries, directorates, and supervisory offices, together with those of Kaifeng Prefecture and the Xingyuan intendant, were all ordered to be recast by Wenrou.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter every seal of the central bureaus, ministries, directorates, and supervisory offices, along with those of Kaifeng Prefecture and the Xingyuan intendant, was entrusted to Wenrou for recasting.

sentences.zh: 太宗雍熙元年，詔新除漢南國王錢俶印，宜以「漢南國」為文。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yongxi of Emperor Taizong, an edict ordered that the seal for the newly appointed King of Hannan, Qian Chu, should bear the inscription 「Hannan Kingdom.」
translations.idiomatic: In Yongxi 1, Taizong decreed that the seal for the newly invested King of Hannan, Qian Chu, should be inscribed with the characters Hannan Kingdom.

sentences.zh: 四年，詔錢俶新授南陽國王印，宜以「南陽國王之印」為文。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, an edict ordered that Qian Chu's newly conferred seal as King of Nanyang should bear the inscription 「Seal of the King of Nanyang Kingdom.」
translations.idiomatic: Four years later Qian Chu received a new seal as King of Nanyang Kingdom, inscribed Seal of the King of Nanyang.

sentences.zh: 真宗咸平三年，賜山前後百蠻王諾驅印，以「大渡河南山前後都鬼王之印」 為文。

translations.literal: In the third year of Xianping of Emperor Zhenzong, a seal was bestowed on Nuoju, king of the hundred barbarians before and behind the mountains, with the inscription 「Seal of the Chief Ghost King before and behind the Mountains south of the Great Crossing.」
translations.idiomatic: In Xianping 3, Zhenzong granted a seal to Nuoju, chief of the hundred barbarian clans before and behind the mountains, inscribed Seal of the Chief Ghost King before and behind the Mountains south of the Dadu River.

sentences.zh: 景德四年，鑄交阯郡王印，製安南旌節，付廣南轉運司就賜之。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Jingde, the seal of the Prince of Jiaozhi Commandery was cast, An Nam banners and tallies were made, and these were entrusted to the Guangnan transport commission for conferral on the spot.
translations.idiomatic: In Jingde 4 a seal for the Prince of Jiaozhi Commandery was cast and An Nam banners and credentials were produced, then handed to the Guangnan transport commission to bestow on the recipient.

sentences.zh: 大中祥符五年，詔諸寺觀及士庶之家所用私記，今後並方一寸，雕木為文，不得私鑄。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Dazhong Xiangfu, an edict ordered that private chops used by temples and commoners' households should thereafter all be one inch square, with characters carved in wood, and private casting was forbidden.
translations.idiomatic: In Dazhong Xiangfu 5 the court ruled that private seals used by temples and common households must hereafter be one inch square, carved in wood only—private metal casting was prohibited.

sentences.zh: 是歲七月，帝覽河西節度使、知許州石普奏狀，用許州觀察使印，以問宰臣王旦。

translations.literal: That year in the seventh month, the emperor reviewed a memorial from Shi Pu, military commissioner of Hexi and prefect of Xuzhou, who had used the Xuzhou observation commissioner seal, and questioned chief minister Wang Dan.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of that year, the emperor read a memorial from Shi Pu, Hexi military commissioner and acting prefect of Xuzhou, sealed with the observation commissioner chop rather than the military commissioner's seal, and asked chief minister Wang Dan whether this was proper.

sentences.zh: 對曰：「節度州有三印：節度印隨本使，使缺則納有司；

translations.literal: He replied: 「A military commission prefecture has three seals: the military commission seal goes with the commissioner; when the commissioner is absent it is surrendered to the appropriate office;
translations.idiomatic: Wang Dan answered: A prefecture that carries a military commission has three seals. The military commission seal travels with the commissioner and is surrendered to the proper office when the post falls vacant;

sentences.zh: 觀察印，則州長吏用之；

translations.literal: the observation seal is used by the prefectural chief official;
translations.idiomatic: the observation seal is kept by the prefect and used by him;

sentences.zh: 州印，晝則付錄事掌用，暮納於長吏。

translations.literal: the prefecture seal is entrusted by day to the recording secretary for use and returned to the chief official at dusk.
translations.idiomatic: the prefecture seal is entrusted each morning to the recording secretary and surrendered back to the chief official each evening.

sentences.zh: 節度使在本鎮，兵仗則節度判官、掌書記、推官書狀，用節度印；
