translations.literal: When the military commissioner is at his headquarters, for military matters the military commission adjutant, chief secretary, and investigating officer draft documents and use the military commission seal;
translations.idiomatic: When the commissioner is at his post, military correspondence drafted by the military adjutant, chief secretary, and investigating officer bears the military commission seal;

sentences.zh: 田賦則觀察判官、支使、推官書狀，用觀察印；

translations.literal: for land tax matters the observation adjutant, administrative aide, and investigating officer draft documents and use the observation seal;
translations.idiomatic: land-tax documents drafted by the observation adjutant, administrative aide, and investigating officer bear the observation seal;

sentences.zh: 符刺屬縣，則本使判書，用州印。

translations.literal: for dispatches and directives to subordinate counties, the commissioner himself passes judgment on documents and uses the prefecture seal.
translations.idiomatic: orders and notices to subordinate counties are judged and signed by the commissioner himself and sealed with the prefecture seal.

sentences.zh: 故命帥必曰某軍節度、某州管內觀察等使、某州刺史。

translations.literal: Therefore when appointing a commander it always states: military commissioner of such-and-such army, observation commissioner within the jurisdiction of such-and-such prefecture, and prefect of such-and-such prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: This is why a territorial commander is always appointed by title as military commissioner of a given army, observation commissioner within a given prefecture, and prefect of that prefecture.

sentences.zh: 言軍，則專制其兵旅；

translations.literal: Speaking of 「army」 means exclusive control over its troops;
translations.idiomatic: The mention of an army denotes sole command over its forces;

sentences.zh: 言管內，則總察其風俗；

translations.literal: speaking of 「within the jurisdiction」 means overall supervision of local customs;
translations.idiomatic: within the jurisdiction denotes authority to oversee local customs throughout the circuit;

sentences.zh: 言刺史，則涖其州事。

translations.literal: speaking of 「prefect」 means presiding over prefectural affairs.
translations.idiomatic: prefect denotes authority to administer the affairs of the prefecture itself.

sentences.zh: 石普獨書奏章，當用河西節度使印。」

translations.literal: Shi Pu alone wrote his memorial; he should have used the Hexi military commissioner seal.」
translations.idiomatic: Shi Pu wrote his memorial unaided and should have affixed the Hexi military commissioner's seal.

sentences.zh: 仁宗景祐三年，少府監言：「得篆文官王文盛狀，『在京三司糧料院，頻有人偽造印記，印成旁曆，盜請官物。

translations.literal: In the third year of Jingyou of Emperor Renzong, the Directorate of Palace Manufactories reported: 「We received a petition from seal-script officer Wang Wensheng: 『At the Three Departments grain rations depot in the capital, people frequently forge seal marks, and after stamping use collateral ledgers to fraudulently draw official goods.
translations.idiomatic: In Jingyou 3 the Directorate of Palace Manufactories reported: We received a petition from seal engraver Wang Wensheng: At the capital's Three Departments grain-ration depot, forgers repeatedly counterfeit official seals and use them to stamp the side ledgers, thus drawing government supplies illicitly.

sentences.zh: 欲乞鑄造圓印三面，每麵闊二寸五分，於外一匝先篆年號及糧料院名，計十二字；

translations.literal: We wish to request casting three round seals, each face two inches and five fen wide; on the outer ring first engrave the reign era and the depot name, totaling twelve characters;
translations.idiomatic: We ask that three round seals be cast, each face two and a half inches wide; the outer band should bear the era name and depot name in twelve characters;

sentences.zh: 次一匝篆寅印十二辰，亦十二字；

translations.literal: on the next ring engrave the twelve Earthly Branches beginning with yin, also twelve characters;
translations.idiomatic: the next band should bear the twelve Earthly Branches beginning with yin, also twelve characters;

sentences.zh: 中心篆正字，上連印鈕，鑄成轉關，以機穴定之。

translations.literal: in the center engrave the correct character, joined above to the seal knob, cast as a rotating mechanism fixed by a slot and pin.
translations.idiomatic: at the center place the active character, connected to the knob above, forged as a rotatable dial locked by a pin and socket.

sentences.zh: 用時逐月分對，年終轉逮十二月，自寅至醜，終始使用。

translations.literal: In use it is matched month by month; by year's end the rotation reaches the twelfth month, used from beginning to end from yin to chou.
translations.idiomatic: In practice the matching character is set month by month; over the year the dial advances through all twelve months, cycling from yin through to chou.

sentences.zh: 所有轉關正字，次月轉定之時，令本院官封押，選差人行使其印。

translations.literal: Whenever the rotating character is set for the next month, depot officials seal and hold it, and selected personnel are dispatched to use the seal.
translations.idiomatic: Each month, when the dial is turned to the new character, depot officers seal and secure it, and designated agents alone may apply the seal.

sentences.zh: 遇改年號，即令別鑄。』

translations.literal: When the era name changes, new seals are to be cast separately.
translations.idiomatic: A change of reign era requires a fresh casting.

sentences.zh: 詔三司定奪以聞，三司請如文盛奏。

translations.literal: 』 An edict ordered the Three Departments to decide and report; the Three Departments requested approval as Wensheng petitioned.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered the Three Departments to adjudicate and report back; they recommended adoption of Wensheng's proposal.

sentences.zh: 後又命知制誥邵必、殿中丞蘇唐卿詳定天下印文，必、唐卿皆通篆籀，然亦無所厘改焉。

translations.literal: Later Shao Bi, drafter of edicts, and Su Tangqing, palace aide, were ordered to examine and settle all seal inscriptions under heaven; both Bi and Tangqing were versed in seal and bronze scripts, yet made no changes whatever.
translations.idiomatic: Later Shao Bi, edict drafter, and Su Tangqing, palace aide, were charged with reviewing every official seal inscription in the realm; both were masters of ancient seal scripts, yet found nothing that required correction.

sentences.zh: 神宗熙寧五年，詔內外官及溪洞官合賜牌印，並令少府監鑄造，送禮部給付。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Xining of Emperor Shenzong, an edict ordered that inner and outer officials and stream-cave officials who should receive plaque-seals should all have them cast by the Directorate of Palace Manufactories and sent to the Ministry of Rites for issuance.
translations.idiomatic: In Xining 5 Shenzong decreed that all inner and outer officials, including stream-cave chieftains entitled to plaque-seals, should receive seals cast by the Palace Manufactories and issued through the Ministry of Rites.

sentences.zh: 元豐三年，廣西經略司言，知南丹州莫世忍貢銀、香、獅子、馬。

translations.literal: In the third year of Yuanfeng, the Guangxi frontier commission reported that Mo Shiren, prefect of Nandan, offered tribute of silver, incense, lions, and horses.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Yuanfeng the Guangxi frontier commission reported that Mo Shiren, magistrate of Nandan Prefecture, had sent tribute of silver, incense, lions, and horses.

sentences.zh: 遂賜以印，以「西南諸道武盛軍德政官家明天國主印」為文，並以南丹州刺史印賜之，仍詔經略司毀其舊印。

translations.literal: Thereupon he was granted a seal bearing 「Seal of the Bright Heaven State Lord of Virtuous Governance, Military Splendor Army of the Southwestern Routes,」 and also granted the Nandan prefect seal; an edict further ordered the frontier commission to destroy his old seal.
translations.idiomatic: Mo Shiren was then granted a seal inscribed Seal of the State Lord of Virtuous Governance, Bright Heaven, Military Splendor Army of the Southwestern Routes, along with the seal of the prefect of Nandan; the frontier commission was ordered to destroy his former seal.

sentences.zh: 六年，舊制貢院專掌貢舉，其印曰「禮部貢舉院之印」，以廢貢院，事歸禮部，別鑄「禮部貢舉之印」。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, under the old system the examination hall exclusively administered examinations, its seal reading 「Seal of the Ministry of Rites Examination Hall」; with abolition of the examination hall and matters returned to the Ministry of Rites, a separate 「Seal of Ministry of Rites Examinations」 was cast.
translations.idiomatic: In year six the examination hall was abolished and its affairs transferred to the Ministry of Rites, which cast a new seal reading Seal of Ministry of Rites Examinations in place of the former Seal of the Ministry of Rites Examination Hall.

sentences.zh: 是歲十二月，詔自今臣僚所授印，亡歿並賜隨葬，不即隨葬因而行用者，論如律。

translations.literal: That year in the twelfth month, an edict ordered that from now on seals conferred on officials, upon death are bestowed for burial with the deceased; those who do not promptly bury them but continue to use them are prosecuted according to law.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month of that year an edict held that official seals should hereafter be buried with their holders upon death; anyone who failed to bury a seal and continued to use it would be punished under the statutes.

sentences.zh: 中興仍舊制，惟三省、樞密院用銀印，六部以下用銅印，諸路監司、州縣亦如之。

translations.literal: After the Restoration the old system continued: only the Three Departments and Bureau of Military Affairs used silver seals, the six ministries and below used bronze seals, and circuit supervisors and prefectures and counties likewise.
translations.idiomatic: After the dynastic revival the former rules held: silver seals for the Three Departments and Military Affairs Bureau, bronze for the six ministries and all lower ranks, and the same for circuit supervisors and local officials.

sentences.zh: 寺監惟長貳給焉，屬則從其長。

translations.literal: For directorates and manufactories only the chief and deputy receive them; subordinates follow their chiefs.
translations.idiomatic: At directorates and manufactories only the director and deputy director received seals; junior staff used their superiors'.

sentences.zh: 若倉庫關涉財用，司存，或給之。

translations.literal: If storehouses involved financial matters, the responsible office might be given one.
translations.idiomatic: Storehouses handling revenue might also be issued seals where the responsible office required them.

sentences.zh: 監司、州縣長官曰印，僚屬曰記。

translations.literal: Circuit supervisors and prefectural and county chief officials called theirs seals; staff members called theirs chops.
translations.idiomatic: Circuit supervisors and prefectural and county chiefs held seals; their subordinates held chops.

sentences.zh: 又下無記者，止令本道給以木朱記，文大方寸。

translations.literal: For those below who had no chop, they were simply given wooden vermilion chops by their circuit, the inscription one square inch.
translations.idiomatic: Officials without chops were issued wooden vermilion seals by their circuit, one square inch in size.

sentences.zh: 或銜命出境者，以奉使印給之，復命則納於有司。

translations.literal: Those bearing imperial commissions abroad were given envoy seals; upon returning to report they surrendered them to the appropriate office.
translations.idiomatic: Envoys bearing imperial commission received mission seals abroad and surrendered them to the proper office upon return.

sentences.zh: 後以朝命出州縣者，亦如之。

translations.literal: Later those departing prefectures and counties on court orders were treated the same.
translations.idiomatic: Officials leaving their posts on court orders were treated likewise.

sentences.zh: 新進士置團司，亦假奉使印，結局還之。

translations.literal: New jinshi appointees forming group offices also borrowed envoy seals and returned them when the assignment concluded.
translations.idiomatic: Newly minted jinshi, when forming group offices, likewise borrowed mission seals and returned them when their duties ended.

sentences.zh: 此常制也。

translations.literal: This was the standing rule.
translations.idiomatic: Such was the standing practice.

sentences.zh: 紹興十四年，臣僚又言：「印信事重，凡有官司印記，年深篆文不明，合改鑄者，非進呈取旨，不得改鑄焉。」

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year of Shaoxing, officials again said: 「Seal credentials are weighty matters; whenever a government office seal has aged until the script is unclear and ought to be recast, without submitting for imperial approval recasting is not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: In Shaoxing 14 officials petitioned again: Seals carry great authority; when any government seal's script has worn illegible and recasting is warranted, no recasting may proceed without submitting the matter for imperial approval.

sentences.zh: 時更鑄者，成都府錢引，每界以銅朱記給之。

translations.literal: 」 At that time what was recast: Chengdu prefecture paper money, each issue given copper vermilion chops.
translations.idiomatic: At that time among items recast were the Chengdu paper-money notes, each issue given its own copper vermilion chop.

sentences.zh: 行在都茶場會子庫，每界給印二十五：國用印三鈕，各以「三省戶房國用司會子印」為文；

translations.literal: At the capital's tea monopoly treasury for paper notes, each issue received twenty-five seals: three knobs for state-use seals, each inscribed 「Seal of the Three Departments Revenue Office State Treasury Paper Notes」;
translations.idiomatic: At the capital's tea monopoly note treasury, each issue received twenty-five seals: three treasury seals inscribed Seal of the Three Departments Revenue Office State Treasury Paper Notes;

sentences.zh: 檢察印五鈕，各以「提領會子庫檢察印」為文；

translations.literal: five knobs for inspection seals, each inscribed 「Seal of the Paper Note Treasury Inspector」;
translations.idiomatic: five inspector's seals inscribed Seal of the Paper Note Treasury Inspector;

sentences.zh: 庫印五鈕，各以「會子庫印造會子印」為文；

translations.literal: five knobs for treasury seals, each inscribed 「Seal of the Paper Note Treasury for Printing Notes」;
translations.idiomatic: five treasury seals inscribed Seal of the Paper Note Treasury for Printing Notes;

sentences.zh: 合同印十二鈕，內一貫文二鈕，各以「會子庫一貫文合同印」為文；

translations.literal: twelve knobs for contract seals, among them two for one-guan denominations, each inscribed 「Paper Note Treasury One-Guan Contract Seal」;
translations.idiomatic: twelve contract seals, including two for one-guan denominations, each inscribed Paper Note Treasury One-Guan Contract Seal;

sentences.zh: 五百文、二百文準此。

translations.literal: Five-hundred-wen and two-hundred-wen denominations followed this rule.
translations.idiomatic: Denominations of five hundred and two hundred wen followed the same pattern.

sentences.zh: 蕃國效順者，給以銅印。

translations.literal: Foreign states that submitted received bronze seals.
translations.idiomatic: Submissive frontier states received bronze seals.

sentences.zh: 安南國王李天祚乞印，以「安南國王之印」六字為文，方二寸，給牌，皆以銅鑄，金塗。

translations.literal: The king of Annam, Li Tianzuo, requested a seal; with the six characters 「Seal of the King of Annam」 as the inscription, two inches square, with plaque; all cast in bronze and gilded.
translations.idiomatic: King Li Tianzuo of Annam petitioned for a seal inscribed with six characters, Seal of the King of Annam, two inches square, with an accompanying plaque—all cast in bronze and gold-plated.

sentences.zh: 西蕃隴右郡王趙懷恩乞印，以「隴右郡王之印」為文給之。

translations.literal: The Hexi Longyou commandery king Zhao Huai'en requested a seal; it was granted with the inscription 「Seal of the Longyou Commandery King.」
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Huai'en, King of Longyou in the western regions, received a seal inscribed Seal of the Longyou Commandery King.

sentences.zh: 宜州界外諸蠻乞印，以「宜州管下羈縻某州之印」為文，凡六十顆給之。

translations.literal: Various barbarians beyond Yizhou's borders requested seals; with the inscription 「Seal of such-and-such loosely governed prefecture under Yizhou」 as the text, sixty in all were granted.
translations.idiomatic: Sixty barbarian chieftains beyond Yizhou received seals inscribed Seal of the such-and-such Loosely Governed Prefecture under Yizhou.

sentences.zh: 其後文武百司節次所鑄，不備載。

translations.literal: Thereafter what was cast in succession by civil and military bureaus is not fully recorded.
translations.idiomatic: Subsequent castings by civil and military offices are not fully recorded here.

sentences.zh: 朱記，同舊制。

translations.literal: Vermilion chops followed the old system.
translations.idiomatic: Vermilion chops remained as under the former regulations.

sentences.zh: 紹興二年，始鑄親賢宅、益王府銅朱記。

translations.literal: In the second year of Shaoxing, copper vermilion chops for the Residence of the Worthy and Kin and the Princely Estate of Yi were first cast.
translations.idiomatic: Shaoxing 2 saw the first casting of copper vermilion chops for the Residence of the Worthy and Kin and the Princely Estate of Yi.

sentences.zh: 二十七年，改鑄建康戶部大軍庫記。

translations.literal: In the twenty-seventh year, the chop for the Jiankang Ministry of Revenue grand army storehouse was recast.
translations.idiomatic: In year twenty-seven the chop of the Jiankang Ministry of Revenue grand army storehouse was recast.

sentences.zh: 三十年，鑄馬軍司統製、統領官朱記。

translations.literal: In the thirtieth year, vermilion chops for horse army command controllers and commanding officers were cast.
translations.idiomatic: Year thirty brought new vermilion chops for the cavalry directorate's controllers and commanding officers.

sentences.zh: 三十二年，鑄鄧、恭、慶王直講、讚讀朱記。

translations.literal: In the thirty-second year, vermilion chops for lecturers and readers of the Princes of Deng, Gong, and Qing were cast.
translations.idiomatic: In year thirty-two vermilion chops were cast for lecturers and readers attached to the Princes of Deng, Gong, and Qing.

sentences.zh: 隆興元年，鑄都督府僉廳記，又鑄寄樁庫記。

translations.literal: In the first year of Longxing, chops for the governor-general's joint secretariat and the reserve treasury were cast.
translations.idiomatic: Longxing 1 brought new chops for the governor-general's joint office and the reserve treasury.

sentences.zh: 二年，鑄戶部大軍庫勘合庫子記二鈕，湖廣總領所覆印會子記二鈕。

translations.literal: In the second year, two knobs of chops for the Ministry of Revenue grand army storehouse verification slips were cast, and two knobs for the Huguang overall command's overprinting note chops.
translations.idiomatic: Longxing 2 added two verification-slip chops for the grand army storehouse and two overprint chops for the Huguang overall command's paper notes.

sentences.zh: 乾道二年，鑄成都錢引務朱記。

translations.literal: In the second year of Qiandao, the Chengdu paper money office vermilion chop was cast.
translations.idiomatic: Qiandao 2 brought a new vermilion chop for the Chengdu paper-money office.

sentences.zh: 淳熙十六年，鑄建康榷貨務中門大門之記。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year of Chunxi, chops for the inner and outer gates of the Jiankang salt and goods monopoly were cast.
translations.idiomatic: Chunxi 16 added chops for the inner and outer gates of the Jiankang salt monopoly office.

sentences.zh: 凡內外官有請於朝，則鑄給焉。

translations.literal: Whenever inner or outer officials petitioned the court, seals were cast and issued.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever inner or outer officials petitioned the court for a seal, one was cast and issued.

sentences.zh: 用木者，易之以銅。

translations.literal: Where wood was used, it was replaced with bronze.
translations.idiomatic: Wooden seals were replaced with bronze ones.

sentences.zh: 符券。

translations.literal: Tallies and credentials.
translations.idiomatic: Tallies and Travel Credentials.

sentences.zh: 唐有銀牌，發驛遣使，則門下省給之。

translations.literal: The Tang had silver plaques; when dispatching envoys via post stations, the Secretariat gave them out.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Tang, silver travel plaques were issued by the Secretariat to envoys using the post relay.

sentences.zh: 其制，闊一寸半，長五寸，麵刻隸字曰「敕走馬銀牌」，凡五字。

translations.literal: Its form: one inch and a half wide, five inches long; the face carved in clerical script with 「Imperial Order Horse-Riding Silver Plaque,」 five characters in all.
translations.idiomatic: Each plaque measured one and a half inches wide and five inches long, the face engraved in clerical script with five characters: Imperial Order Horse-Riding Silver Plaque.

sentences.zh: 首為竅，貫以韋帶。

translations.literal: The head had a hole, strung on a leather cord.
translations.idiomatic: A hole at the head allowed it to be threaded onto a leather cord.

sentences.zh: 其後罷之。

translations.literal: Later it was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: The practice was later abolished.

sentences.zh: 宋初，令樞密院給券，謂之「頭子」。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Song, the Military Affairs Bureau was ordered to issue credentials, called 「touzi.」
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Song, the Military Affairs Bureau issued credentials known as touzi.

sentences.zh: 太宗太平興國三年，李飛雄詐乘驛謀亂，伏誅。

translations.literal: In the third year of Taiping Xingguo of Emperor Taizong, Li Feixiong fraudulently used the post relay to plot rebellion and was executed.
translations.idiomatic: In Taiping Xingguo 3 Li Feixiong forged post credentials to plot rebellion and was executed.

sentences.zh: 詔罷樞密院券，乘驛者復製銀牌，闊二寸半，長六寸。

translations.literal: An edict abolished Military Affairs Bureau credentials; post relay users again made silver plaques, two and a half inches wide and six inches long.
translations.idiomatic: The court abolished Military Affairs credentials and restored silver plaques for post travelers, two and a half inches wide and six inches long.

sentences.zh: 易以八分書，上鈒二飛鳳，下鈒二麒麟，兩邊年月，貫以紅絲絛。

translations.literal: Changed to eight-part script; two flying phoenixes stamped above, two qilin below, year and month on both sides, threaded with a red silk cord.
translations.idiomatic: They were inscribed in eight-part script, stamped above with twin flying phoenixes and below with twin qilin, dated on both margins, and threaded with a red silk cord.

sentences.zh: 端拱中，以使臣護邊兵多遺失，又罷銀牌，復給樞密院券。

translations.literal: During the Duan Gong era, because frontier-guard envoys frequently lost them, silver plaques were again abolished and Military Affairs Bureau credentials restored.
translations.idiomatic: During Duan Gong, frontier envoys lost their plaques so often that silver plaques were abolished once more and Military Affairs credentials restored.

sentences.zh: 仁宗康定元年五月，翰林學士承旨丁度、翰林學士王堯臣、知制誥葉清臣等請製軍中傳信牌及兵符事，詔令兩製與端明殿學士李淑詳定，奏聞：

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the first year of Kangding of Emperor Renzong, Hanlin academician recipient of edicts Ding Du, Hanlin academician Wang Kuchen, edict drafter Ye Qingchen and others requested manufacture of army message boards and military tally matters; an edict ordered the two academies and Hall of Enlightened Governance academician Li Shu to examine and decide, reporting:
translations.idiomatic: In Kangding 1, fifth month, chief Hanlin academicians Ding Du and Wang Kuchen and edict drafter Ye Qingchen petitioned for army signal boards and military tallies; the emperor charged the two academies and Li Shu, academician of the Hall of Enlightened Governance, to draft specifications and report back:

sentences.zh: 軍中符信，切要杜絕奸詐，深合機宜。

translations.literal: Army tallies and credentials must strictly cut off fraud and deceit; this deeply suits strategic needs.
translations.idiomatic: Military credentials must above all forestall fraud—requirements that fit the exigencies of the field.

sentences.zh: 今請下有司造銅兵符，給諸路總管主將，每發兵三百人或全指揮以上即用。

translations.literal: We now request ordering the relevant offices to cast bronze military tallies, issuing them to route commanders-in-chief; whenever deploying three hundred troops or a full command or more they are used.
translations.idiomatic: We ask that bronze military tallies be cast and issued to each route's commander-in-chief, to be used whenever three hundred men or an entire command is mobilized.

sentences.zh: 又別造傳信朱漆木牌，給應軍中往來之處，每傳達號令、關報會合及發兵三百人以下即用。

translations.literal: Also separately make vermilion-lacquered wooden message boards for all places of army comings and goings; whenever conveying orders, reporting for rendezvous, or deploying fewer than three hundred troops they are used.
translations.idiomatic: Separate vermilion-lacquered wooden signal boards should serve every point of military traffic—for relaying orders, rendezvous reports, and mobilizations of fewer than three hundred men.

sentences.zh: 又檢到符彥卿《軍律》有字驗，亦乞令於移牒、傳信牌上，兩處參驗使用。

translations.literal: Also we found that Fu Yanqing's Military Regulations contains character verification; we also request ordering its use on dispatches and signal boards, verified at both places.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Yanqing's Military Regulations preserves a system of coded verification characters; we ask that these be applied on dispatches and signal boards and cross-checked at both ends.

sentences.zh: 一、銅兵符：漢制，銅鑄，上刻虎形。

translations.literal: One, bronze military tallies: Han system, cast in bronze, carved above with tiger form.
translations.idiomatic: I. Bronze military tallies: under the Han system these were cast in bronze and carved with a tiger form.

sentences.zh: 今聞皇城司見有木魚契，乞令有司用木契形狀，精巧鑄造。

translations.literal: We now hear the Imperial City Bureau has wooden fish tallies; we request ordering the relevant offices to use the wooden tally form and cast them with fine craftsmanship.
translations.idiomatic: The Imperial City Bureau still holds wooden fish tallies; we ask that new ones be finely cast to that same shape.

sentences.zh: 陝西五路，每路依漢制各給一至二十，計二十麵，更換給用，仍以公牒為照驗。

translations.literal: In the five routes of Shaanxi, each route according to Han practice is given one to twenty, totaling twenty faces, replaced and issued in rotation, still using official dispatches as verification.
translations.idiomatic: For Shaanxi's five routes, each route should receive one to twenty tallies under the Han precedent, twenty faces in all, rotated in issue, with official dispatches retained for verification.

sentences.zh: 二、傳信木牌：先朝舊制，合用堅木朱漆為之，長六寸，闊三寸，腹背刻字而中分之，字雲某路傳信牌。

translations.literal: Two, message wooden boards: former court old system, properly made of hard wood with vermilion lacquer, six inches long, three inches wide; front and back carved with characters and split down the middle; characters say 「such-and-such route message board.」
translations.idiomatic: II. Wooden signal boards: under the former court's practice these were of hard wood lacquered vermilion, six inches long and three inches wide, inscribed on both faces and split down the middle, bearing the legend Signal Board of the Such-and-Such Route.

sentences.zh: 卻置池槽，牙縫相合。

translations.literal: Reversed, a groove and slot were set so the teeth fit together.
translations.idiomatic: Each half was grooved so that its serrated edge mated perfectly with the other.

sentences.zh: 又鑿二竅，置筆墨，上帖紙，書所傳達事。

translations.literal: Also two holes were bored, ink and brush placed inside; paper pasted on top recording what was conveyed.
translations.idiomatic: Two cavities were cut to hold ink and brush; paper was affixed on top to record the message.

sentences.zh: 用印印號上，以皮係往來軍吏之項。

translations.literal: A seal mark was stamped on the number; leather cord tied around the neck of the traveling army clerk.
translations.idiomatic: The seal was applied to the serial number and a leather cord was tied around the traveling officer's neck.

sentences.zh: 臨陣傳言，應有取索，並以此牌為言，寫其上。

translations.literal: On the battlefield when relaying messages, for any requisition, all used this board as the vehicle, writing upon it.
translations.idiomatic: Battlefield orders and requisitions were likewise written on the board.

sentences.zh: 如已曉會施行訖，復書牌上遣回。

translations.literal: If understanding was reached and execution completed, a reply was written on the board and sent back.
translations.idiomatic: Once orders were understood and carried out, a reply was written on the board and the messenger sent back.

sentences.zh: 今乞下有司造牌，每路各給一面為樣，餘令本司依此制造，分給諸處，更換使用。

translations.literal: We now request ordering the relevant offices to make boards; each route given one as a model, the rest ordered made by their bureau according to this, distributed to various places, rotated in use.
translations.idiomatic: We ask that the relevant offices manufacture boards, issue one sample to each route, and have each bureau produce the rest for distribution and rotation.

sentences.zh: 城砦分屯軍馬，事須往來關會之處，亦如數給與。

translations.literal: Fortresses and stockades garrisoning troops separately, wherever comings and goings require coordination, should likewise be given them in proportion.
translations.idiomatic: Garrison posts requiring coordination should receive them in corresponding numbers.

sentences.zh: 三、字驗：凡軍行計會，不免文牒，或主司遺失懼罪，單使被擒，軍中所謀，自然泄露。

translations.literal: Three, character verification: whenever armies march and must coordinate, documents cannot be avoided; if a responsible officer lost them fearing punishment, or a lone messenger was captured, whatever the army plotted would naturally leak.
translations.idiomatic: III. Coded verification characters: armies cannot coordinate without written orders; if an officer lost a dispatch in fear of punishment, or a lone courier was taken, every plan would be exposed.

sentences.zh: 故每分屯軍馬之時，與主將密定字號，各掌一通，不令左右人知其義理。

translations.literal: Therefore whenever troops were garrisoned separately, with the commander-in-chief they secretly fixed code characters, each keeping one copy, not letting attendants know their meaning.
translations.idiomatic: Before troops were posted separately, the commander and his subordinate secretly agreed on coded characters, each keeping one copy unknown even to their attendants.

sentences.zh: 但於尋常公狀文移內，以此字私為契約，有所施行，依此參驗。

translations.literal: Only in ordinary official documents and correspondence, using these characters privately as covenant, whatever was enacted, was verified according to this.
translations.idiomatic: In routine official correspondence these characters served as a private pact; any action taken was verified against them.

sentences.zh: 不得字有重疊，及用凶惡嫌疑之語。

translations.literal: Characters must not overlap, nor use ominous or suspicious language.
translations.idiomatic: Duplicate characters and ominous or incriminating phrases were forbidden.

sentences.zh: 每用文牒之上，別行寫此字驗，訖，印其上發往。

translations.literal: On each document used, this character verification was written separately; when finished, stamped upon it and sent out.
translations.idiomatic: Each dispatch bore the verification character written separately below the main text, then sealed and dispatched.

sentences.zh: 如所請報，到，許，即依號卻寫印遣回；

translations.literal: If what was requested was reported, arrived, approved, then according to the code a reply was written, stamped, and sent back;
translations.idiomatic: If the request arrived and was approved, a coded reply was written, sealed, and returned;

sentences.zh: 如不許，即空之。

translations.literal: if not approved, it was left blank.
translations.idiomatic: if denied, the reply space was left blank.

sentences.zh: 此惟主將自知，他人皆不得測。

translations.literal: Only the commander-in-chief knew this himself; others could not guess.
translations.idiomatic: Only the commanding general knew the code; no one else could fathom it.

sentences.zh: 符彥卿元用四十條，以四十字為號；

translations.literal: Fu Yanqing originally used forty articles, taking forty characters as the designation;
translations.idiomatic: Fu Yanqing had originally drafted forty articles, keyed to a forty-character mnemonic phrase;

sentences.zh: 今檢得隻有三十七條，內亦有不急之事，今減作二十八字。

translations.literal: Now upon inspection there are only thirty-seven articles, among which are also matters not urgent; now they are reduced to twenty-eight characters.
translations.idiomatic: An audit found only thirty-seven items left, some of them nonessential, so the code was shortened to twenty-eight characters.

sentences.zh: 所貴軍中戎旅之人，事簡易記。

translations.literal: What is valued is that army personnel in the ranks find affairs simple and easy to remember.
translations.idiomatic: The aim was to keep things simple enough for soldiers in the field to memorize.

sentences.zh: 詔並從之。

translations.literal: An edict approved all of this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered that all these changes be adopted.

sentences.zh: 嘉祐四年，三司使張方平編驛券則例，凡七十四條，賜名《嘉祐驛令》。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Jiayou, the Commissioner of the Three Departments Zhang Fangping compiled regulations for relay passes, seventy-four articles in all, and it was granted the name "Jiayou Relay Regulations."
translations.idiomatic: In Jiayou 4, Zhang Fangping, head of the Three Departments, codified seventy-four rules for courier vouchers, issued under the title Jiayou Relay Regulations.

sentences.zh: 神宗熙寧五年，詔西作坊鑄造諸銅符三十四副，令三司給左契付諸門，右契付大內鑰匙庫。

translations.literal: In the 5th year of Xining under Emperor Shenzong, an edict ordered the Western Workshop to cast thirty-four pairs of copper tally tokens; the Three Departments were to issue the left halves to the various gates, and the right halves to the Grand Inner Palace Key Repository.
translations.idiomatic: In Xining 5 (1072), Shenzong ordered the Western Workshop to cast thirty-four matched sets of bronze gate tallies—the left tokens issued through the Three Departments to each city gate, the right tokens kept in the inner palace key vault.

sentences.zh: 今後諸門輪差人員，依時轉銅契入，赴庫勘同。

translations.literal: Henceforth personnel rotated among the various gates shall, according to schedule, exchange the copper tallies and enter, going to the repository to verify matching halves.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter, gate guards on rotation would bring in their bronze tally on schedule and have it verified against the vault's matching half.

sentences.zh: 其鐵牌隻請人自執，在外仗止宿。

translations.literal: As for the iron plaques, only the requester himself holds them; the outer guard detachment billets outside.
translations.idiomatic: The iron pass plaques stayed in the hands of whoever requested entry, while the outer watch remained encamped outside.

sentences.zh: 本庫依漏刻發鑰匙，付外仗驗請人鐵牌給付，候開門訖，卻執鐵牌納鑰匙，請出銅契。

translations.literal: The repository, according to the clepsydra schedule, releases keys, entrusting the outer guard to inspect the requester's iron plaque before handing them over; after the gate opening is complete, one then holds the iron plaque to return the keys and requests release of the copper tally.
translations.idiomatic: The vault dispensed keys on the water-clock schedule only after the outer guard confirmed the requester's iron plaque; once the gate had opened and closed, the plaque was returned with the keys to retrieve the bronze tally.

sentences.zh: 至晚卻依上請納。

translations.literal: By evening one again follows the above procedure to request and return.
translations.idiomatic: The same exchange was repeated at nightfall.

sentences.zh: 其開門朝牌六面，亦隨銅契依舊發放。

translations.literal: The six morning gate-opening plaques were also issued according to the old practice along with the copper tallies.
translations.idiomatic: Six daybreak gate plaques were still issued along with the bronzes, as before.

sentences.zh: 時神宗以京城門禁不嚴，素無符契，命樞密院約舊制，更造銅契，中刻魚形，以門名識之，分左右給納，以戒不虞，而啟閉之法密於舊矣。

translations.literal: At that time Shenzong, because capital gate security was lax and there had long been no tally tokens, ordered the Bureau of Military Affairs to follow the old system, newly cast copper tallies, carved with fish shapes in the center, marked with gate names, divided into left and right for issue and return, to guard against the unexpected—and the methods of opening and closing grew stricter than before.
translations.idiomatic: Shenzong had found the capital's gates poorly controlled and long without formal tallies, so he charged the Bureau of Military Affairs with reviving the old custom: new bronze tokens, fish-shaped at the split, engraved with each gate's name, left and right halves issued and surrendered separately—all to forestall surprise, and gate discipline became tighter than ever.

sentences.zh: 元豐元年，詳定禮文所言：「舊南郊式，車駕出入宣德門、太廟靈星門、朱雀門、南薰門，皆勘箭。

translations.literal: In the 1st year of Yuanfeng, the committee for determining ritual texts stated: "In the old Southern Suburban rite, when the imperial carriage entered or exited Xuande Gate, the Spirit Star Gate of the Imperial Ancestral Temple, Zhuque Gate, and Nanxun Gate, all were subject to tally-arrow inspection.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Yuanfeng (1078), the ritual reform commission argued: "Under the old Southern Suburban rite, whenever the imperial procession passed Xuande Gate, the Imperial Temple's Lingxing Gate, Zhuque Gate, or Nanxun Gate, guards checked tally arrows.

sentences.zh: 熙寧中，因參知政事王珪議，已罷勘箭，而勘契之式尚存。

translations.literal: In the Xining period, because of Vice Grand Counselor Wang Gui's proposal, tally-arrow inspection had already been abolished, but the form of tally-token inspection still remained.
translations.idiomatic: During Xining, at Vice Grand Counselor Wang Gui's urging, the arrow check had been dropped, though the token check remained on the books.

sentences.zh: 《春秋》之義，不敢以所不信加之尊者；

translations.literal: The principle of the Spring and Autumn Annals is that one dare not impose upon one's superior what one does not believe in;
translations.idiomatic: The teaching of the Spring and Autumn Annals holds that one must not burden a sovereign with rituals one does not oneself trust;

sentences.zh: 且雷動天行，無容疑貳，必使誰何而後過門，不應典禮。

translations.literal: Moreover, when thunder moves and Heaven proceeds, there is no room for doubt or second thoughts; to require questioning and identification before passing the gate does not accord with canonical ritual.
translations.idiomatic: When heaven itself marches forth like rolling thunder, no rite should admit doubt or hesitation—making an emperor identify himself at a gate is simply unbecoming.

sentences.zh: 考詳事始，不見於《開寶禮》。

translations.literal: Examining the matter in detail, it is not found in the Kaibao Ritual.
translations.idiomatic: A close review traced the practice to no authority in the Kaibao Ritual.

sentences.zh: 咸平中，初載於儀注，蓋當時禮官之失。

translations.literal: In the Xianping period it first appeared in ritual manuals—likely a lapse on the part of the ritual officials of that time.
translations.idiomatic: It first entered the ceremonial manuals in the Xianping era—a mistake by the ritualists of that day, in all likelihood.

sentences.zh: 請自今車駕出入，罷勘契。」

translations.literal: We request that from now on, when the imperial carriage enters or exits, tally-token inspection be abolished.
translations.idiomatic: We recommend abolishing token checks whenever the imperial carriage passes hereafter.

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: [The emperor] approved.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 高宗建炎三年，改鑄虎符，樞密院主之。

translations.literal: In the 3rd year of Jianyan under Gaozong, tiger tallies were recast; the Bureau of Military Affairs supervised the matter.
translations.idiomatic: In Jianyan 3 (1129), Gaozong ordered new tiger tallies cast under Bureau of Military Affairs supervision.

sentences.zh: 其制以銅為之，長六寸，闊三寸，刻篆而中分之，以左契給諸路，右契藏之。

translations.literal: Its form was made of copper, six inches long and three inches wide, engraved in seal script and split down the middle; the left half was given to the various circuits, the right half kept in store.
translations.idiomatic: Each was cast bronze, six by three inches, seal-scripted and split: left halves to the circuits, right halves locked in the bureau vault.

sentences.zh: 門符製，以繒裹紙版，謂之「號」，皇城司掌之。

translations.literal: The design of gate tokens: silk-wrapped paper boards, called "hao," administered by the Imperial City Office.
translations.idiomatic: Gate passes took the form of silk-wrapped paper slips called hao, kept by the Imperial City Office.

sentences.zh: 敕入禁衛號，黃綾八角，三千道；

translations.literal: Edict-entering forbidden guard tokens: yellow damask, octagonal, three thousand pieces;
translations.idiomatic: For imperial edicts entering the inner guard: three thousand octagonal yellow-silk passes;

sentences.zh: 入殿門黃絹以方，一千道；

translations.literal: Entering hall gates—yellow silk, square shape, one thousand pieces;
translations.idiomatic: For hall gates: one thousand square yellow-silk passes;

sentences.zh: 入宮門黃絹以圓，八千道；

translations.literal: Entering palace gates—yellow silk, round shape, eight thousand pieces;
translations.idiomatic: For palace gates: eight thousand round yellow-silk passes;

sentences.zh: 入皇城門黃絹以長，三千道。

translations.literal: Entering imperial city gates—yellow silk, elongated shape, three thousand pieces.
translations.idiomatic: For imperial city gates: three thousand oblong yellow-silk passes.

sentences.zh: 紹興二年正月所定也。

translations.literal: This was fixed in the first month of the 2nd year of Shaoxing.
translations.idiomatic: These quotas were set in the first month of Shaoxing 2 (1132).

sentences.zh: 後更宮門號以緋紅絹方，皇城門以緋紅絹圓，遂久用之。

translations.literal: Later the palace gate tokens were changed to scarlet silk, square; imperial city gate tokens to scarlet silk, round—and these were used for a long time.
translations.idiomatic: Later, square scarlet passes marked palace gates and round scarlet passes the imperial city gates—a scheme kept in use for years.

sentences.zh: 後復盡以黃，或方或圓，各隨其制。

translations.literal: Later they again all reverted to yellow, square or round according to each type's regulation.
translations.idiomatic: Eventually everything went back to yellow again, square or round as each gate required.

sentences.zh: 又有檄牌，其制有金字牌、青字牌、紅字牌。

translations.literal: There were also dispatch plaques; their forms included gold-character plaques, green-character plaques, and red-character plaques.
translations.idiomatic: Dispatch plaques came in three grades: gold-letter, green-letter, and red-letter.

sentences.zh: 金字牌者，日行四百里，郵置之最速遞也；

translations.literal: Gold-character plaques traveled four hundred li per day—the fastest relay of the postal stations;
translations.idiomatic: Gold-letter plaques, the swiftest couriers of the post system, covered four hundred li a day;

sentences.zh: 凡赦書及軍機要切則用之，由內侍省發遣焉。

translations.literal: They were used for all amnesty edicts and urgent military matters, dispatched by the Palace Domestic Service.
translations.idiomatic: Reserved for amnesties and urgent military business, they were issued by the Palace Domestic Service.

sentences.zh: 乾道末，樞密院置雌黃青字牌，日行三百五十里，軍期急速則用之。

translations.literal: At the end of Qiandao, the Bureau of Military Affairs established ochre-green-character plaques, traveling three hundred fifty li per day, used when military deadlines were extremely urgent.
translations.idiomatic: Late in Qiandao (1170s), the Bureau added ochre-green-letter plaques at three hundred fifty li a day for pressing military deadlines.

sentences.zh: 淳熙末，趙汝愚在樞筦，乃作黑漆紅字牌，奏委諸路提舉官催督，歲校遲速最甚者，以議賞罰。

translations.literal: At the end of Chunxi, Zhao Ruyu while at the Bureau of Military Affairs then made black-lacquer red-character plaques, memorialized to entrust circuit intendant officials to urge and supervise; annually the slowest and fastest were compared to propose rewards and punishments.
translations.idiomatic: Near the end of Chunxi (1180s), Zhao Ruyu at the Bureau introduced black lacquer plaques with red lettering and had circuit intendants enforce delivery times—each year the worst and best performers were singled out for discipline or reward.

sentences.zh: 其後尚書省亦踵行之，仍命逐州通判具出入界日時狀申省。

translations.literal: Thereafter the Department of State Affairs also followed suit, additionally ordering each prefecture's vice-prefect to submit reports stating the dates and times of entry and exit at boundaries to the Department.
translations.idiomatic: The Department of State Affairs soon copied the practice, requiring each prefecture's vice-prefect to file boundary crossing times with the capital.

sentences.zh: 久之，稽緩復如故。

translations.literal: After a long time, delays once again returned to the old ways.
translations.idiomatic: In time, sluggish deliveries returned as before.

sentences.zh: 紹熙末，遂置擺鋪焉。

translations.literal: At the end of Shaoxi, relay stations were then established for this purpose.
translations.idiomatic: By the end of Shaoxi (1190s), dedicated courier relay stations were set up to address the problem.

sentences.zh: 宮室。

translations.literal: Palaces and halls.
translations.idiomatic: Palace Architecture.

sentences.zh: 汴宋之制，侈而不可以訓。

translations.literal: The institutions of Northern Song Bianjing were extravagant and could not serve as a model for instruction.
translations.idiomatic: Kaifeng under the Northern Song had been lavish beyond any useful precedent.

sentences.zh: 中興，服御惟務簡省，宮殿尤樸。

translations.literal: After the Restoration, apparel and equipage strove solely for simplicity and austerity; palaces were especially plain.
translations.idiomatic: After the restoration, the court stripped ceremony to essentials—and the palaces were deliberately spare.

sentences.zh: 皇帝之居曰殿，總曰大內，又曰南內，本杭州治也。

translations.literal: The emperor's residence was called a hall; collectively it was called the Grand Inner Palace, also called the Southern Inner Palace—it had originally been Hangzhou's administrative seat.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor lived in halls collectively known as the Grand Inner Palace or Southern Inner—formerly Hangzhou's government compound.

sentences.zh: 紹興初，創為之。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Shaoxing it was first established.
translations.idiomatic: It was first adapted at the start of the Shaoxing era (1131).

sentences.zh: 休兵後，始作崇政、垂拱二殿。

translations.literal: After the cessation of warfare, the Chongzheng and Chuigong Halls were first built.
translations.idiomatic: Once fighting ceased, the Chongzheng and Chuigong halls were erected.

sentences.zh: 久之，又作天章等六閣。

translations.literal: After a long time, the Tianzhang and five other pavilions were also built.
translations.idiomatic: Later came six pavilions including Tianzhang.

sentences.zh: 寢殿曰福寧殿。

translations.literal: The sleeping hall was called Funing Hall.
translations.idiomatic: The private quarters were the Funing Hall.

sentences.zh: 淳熙初，孝宗始作射殿，謂之選德殿。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Chunxi, Xiaozong first built an archery hall, called Xuande Hall.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Chunxi, Xiaozong added an archery hall named Xuande.

sentences.zh: 八年秋，又改後殿擁舍為別殿，取舊名，謂之延和殿，便坐視事則禦之。

translations.literal: In the autumn of the 8th year, the rear hall's attached chambers were again converted into a separate hall, taking an old name and calling it Yanhe Hall; for informal sessions handling affairs one resided there.
translations.idiomatic: In the autumn of Chunxi 8 (1181), the rear annex was refitted as Yanhe Hall, bearing an old name—Xiaozong used it for everyday audiences.

sentences.zh: 他如紫宸、文德、集英、大慶、講武，惟隨時所禦，則易其名。

translations.literal: Others such as Zichen, Wende, Jiying, Daqing, and Jiangwu—only according to what was used at the time would their names be changed.
translations.idiomatic: Halls like Zichen, Wende, Jiying, Daqing, and Jiangwu were renamed on the spot according to whatever function they served that day.

sentences.zh: 紫宸殿，遇朔受朝則禦焉；

translations.literal: Zichen Hall—when receiving court audience on the first of the month, one resided there;
translations.idiomatic: Zichen Hall hosted the first-of-the-month audience;

sentences.zh: 文德殿，降赦則禦焉；

translations.literal: Wende Hall—when issuing amnesties, one resided there;
translations.idiomatic: Wende Hall for amnesty proclamations;

sentences.zh: 集英殿，臨軒策士則禦焉；

translations.literal: Jiying Hall—when holding imperial-examination essays before the throne, one resided there;
translations.idiomatic: Jiying Hall for palace examinations;

sentences.zh: 大慶殿，行冊禮則禦焉；

translations.literal: Daqing Hall—when conducting investiture rites, one resided there;
translations.idiomatic: Daqing Hall for investiture ceremonies;

sentences.zh: 講武殿，閱武則禦焉。

translations.literal: Jiangwu Hall—when reviewing troops, one resided there.
translations.idiomatic: Jiangwu Hall for military reviews.

sentences.zh: 其實垂拱、崇政二殿，權更其號而已。

translations.literal: In truth the Chuigong and Chongzheng two halls were merely temporarily changing their designations, that is all.
translations.idiomatic: In effect, Chongzheng and Chuigong were simply the same halls under rotating names.

sentences.zh: 二殿雖曰大殿，其脩廣僅如大郡之設廳。

translations.literal: Although the two halls were called great halls, their length and width were only like the audience halls set up in a large prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Though dubbed "great halls," both were no larger than a major prefecture's main reception room.

sentences.zh: 淳熙再修，止循其舊。

translations.literal: When rebuilt in Chunxi, they simply followed the old dimensions.
translations.idiomatic: A Chunxi-era renovation changed nothing in their scale.

sentences.zh: 每殿為屋五間，十二架，脩六丈，廣八丈四尺。

translations.literal: Each hall was five bays of building, twelve purlin-frames, six zhang in length and eight zhang four chi in width.
translations.idiomatic: Each hall spanned five bays on twelve roof frames—six by eight and four-tenths zhang.

sentences.zh: 殿南簷屋三間，脩一丈五尺，廣亦如之。

translations.literal: South of the hall eaves, a three-bay building, one zhang five chi in length, equal in width.
translations.idiomatic: A three-bay south-eaves annex measured one and a half zhang square.

sentences.zh: 兩朵殿各二間，東西廊各二十間，南廊九間。

translations.literal: Two flanking halls each of two bays; east and west corridors each of twenty bays; south corridor of nine bays.
translations.idiomatic: Flanking annexes held two bays apiece; east and west corridors ran twenty bays each, the south corridor nine.

sentences.zh: 其中為殿門，三間六架，脩三丈，廣四丈六尺。

translations.literal: In the center was the hall gate, three bays and six frames, three zhang in length and four zhang six chi in width.
translations.idiomatic: The central gate hall stood three bays wide on six frames—three by four and six-tenths zhang.

sentences.zh: 殿後擁舍七間，即為延和，其制尤卑，陛階一級，小如常人所居而已。

translations.literal: Behind the hall, attached chambers of seven bays—that was Yanhe—its form especially low; the stair platform had one step, small like an ordinary person's dwelling, that is all.
translations.idiomatic: Seven rear annex bays became Yanhe—deliberately modest, a single step up, no grander than a commoner's house.

sentences.zh: 奉太上則有德壽宮、重華宮、壽康宮，奉聖母則有慈寧宮、慈福宮、壽慈宮。

translations.literal: For serving the Retired Emperor there were De Shou Palace, Chonghua Palace, and Shoukang Palace; for serving the Empress Dowager there were Cining Palace, Cifu Palace, and Shouci Palace.
translations.idiomatic: Retired emperors were lodged at De Shou, Chonghua, or Shoukang; empress dowagers at Cining, Cifu, or Shouci.

sentences.zh: 德壽宮在大內北望仙橋，故又謂之北內，紹興三十二年所造，宮成，詔以德壽宮為名，高宗為上皇禦之。

translations.literal: De Shou Palace was north of Wangxian Bridge within the Grand Inner Palace, hence it was also called the Northern Inner Palace; built in the 32nd year of Shaoxing, when the palace was completed an edict named it De Shou Palace, and Gaozong as Retired Emperor resided there.
translations.idiomatic: De Shou Palace stood north of Wangxian Bridge in the inner precinct—the Northern Inner, erected in Shaoxing 32 (1162); when finished, Gaozong took up residence there as retired emperor.

sentences.zh: 重華宮即德壽宮也，孝宗遜位禦之。

translations.literal: Chonghua Palace was De Shou Palace; Xiaozong upon abdicating resided there.
translations.idiomatic: Chonghua was the same as De Shou—where Xiaozong lived after abdicating.

sentences.zh: 壽康宮即寧福殿也。

translations.literal: Shoukang Palace was Ningfu Hall.
translations.idiomatic: Shoukang Palace was originally Ningfu Hall.

sentences.zh: 初，丞相趙汝愚議以秘書省為泰寧宮，已而不果行，以慈懿皇后外第為之。

translations.literal: At first Grand Counselor Zhao Ruyu proposed using the Secretariat as Taining Palace, but this was not carried out; instead the Empress Dowager Ciyi's outer residence was used.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Counselor Zhao Ruyu had first proposed converting the Secretariat into Taining Palace, but the plan fell through; Empress Dowager Ciyi's suburban mansion was used instead.

sentences.zh: 上皇不欲遷，因以舊寧福殿為壽康宮，光宗遜位禦之。

translations.literal: The Retired Emperor did not wish to move; therefore the old Ningfu Hall was made Shoukang Palace, and Guangzong upon abdicating resided there.
translations.idiomatic: The retired emperor refused to relocate, so the old Ningfu Hall became Shoukang—Guangzong's home after abdication.

sentences.zh: 大內苑中，亭殿亦無增，其名稱可見者，僅有復古殿、損齋、觀堂、芙蓉閣、翠寒堂、清華閣、欏木堂、隱岫、澄碧、倚桂、隱秀、碧琳堂之類，此南內也。

translations.literal: Within the garden of the Grand Inner, pavilions and halls likewise had no additions; the names that appear include only Fugu Hall, Sunzhai, Guantang, Furong Pavilion, Cuihan Hall, Qinghua Pavilion, Luomu Hall, Hidden Peak, Clear Jade, Leaning Cassia, Hidden Splendor, Bilin Hall, and the like—this is the Southern Inner.
translations.idiomatic: The Southern Inner garden gained few new structures; surviving names include Fugu Hall, Sunzhai, Guantang, Furong Pavilion, Cuihan Hall, Qinghua Pavilion, Luomu Hall, Hidden Peak, Clear Pool, Cassia Leaning, Hidden Splendor, and Bilin Hall.

sentences.zh: 北內苑中，則有大池，引西湖水注之，其上疊石為山，象飛來峰。

translations.literal: Within the Northern Inner garden there was a great pond; West Lake water was drawn in to fill it; upon it piled stones formed a mountain, imitating Feilai Peak.
translations.idiomatic: The Northern Inner garden held a great pond fed by West Lake water, with a rockery modeled on Feilai Peak.

sentences.zh: 有樓曰聚遠，禁籞周回，四分之。

translations.literal: There was a tower called Juyuan; the forbidden enclosure circled around, one quarter of it.
translations.idiomatic: A tower called Gather-Distant stood within an imperial enclosure that occupied a quarter of the grounds.

sentences.zh: 東則香遠、清深、月台、梅坡、鬆菊三徑、清妍、清新、芙蓉岡，南則載忻、欣欣、射廳、臨賦、燦錦、至樂、半丈紅、清曠、瀉碧，西則冷泉、文杏館、靜樂、浣溪，北則絳華、旱船、俯翠、春桃、盤鬆。

translations.literal: To the east were Xiangyuan, Qingshen, Yuetai, Meipo, Songju Sanjing, Qingyan, Qingxin, Furonggang; to the south Zaixin, Xinxin, Sheting, Linfu, Canjin, Zhile, Banzhanghong, Qingkuang, Xiebi; to the west Lengquan, Wenxingguan, Jingyue, Huanxi; to the north Jianghua, Hanchuan, Fucui, Chuntao, Pansong.
translations.idiomatic: East held Fragrant Distance, Clear Depth, Moon Terrace, Plum Slope, Pine-and-Chrysanthemum Three Paths, and others; south, Zaixin, Radiant Joy, archery hall, Linfu, Brocade Blaze, Supreme Delight, Half-Zhang Red, Clear Vista, and Pouring Jade; west, Cold Spring, Apricot Lodge, Quiet Joy, and Brook Washing; north, Crimson Bloom, Dry Boat, Bowing to Green, Spring Peach, and Coiled Pine.

sentences.zh: 皇太子宮曰東宮。

translations.literal: The Crown Prince's palace was called the Eastern Palace.
translations.idiomatic: The heir apparent's residence was the Eastern Palace.

sentences.zh: 其未出閣，但聽讀於資善堂，堂在宮門內。

translations.literal: Before leaving the palace for his own establishment, he only listened to lectures at Zishan Hall; the hall was inside the palace gate.
translations.idiomatic: Before coming of age, the prince studied at Zishan Hall just inside the palace gates.

sentences.zh: 已受冊，則居東宮，宮在麗正門內。

translations.literal: Once invested, he then resided in the Eastern Palace; the palace was inside Lizheng Gate.
translations.idiomatic: After investiture he moved to the Eastern Palace within Lizheng Gate.

sentences.zh: 紹興三十二年始置，孝宗居之；

translations.literal: First established in the 32nd year of Shaoxing; Xiaozong resided there;
translations.idiomatic: Established in Shaoxing 32 (1162), where Xiaozong had lived as prince;

sentences.zh: 莊文太子立，復居之。

translations.literal: When Crown Prince Zhuangwen was established, he again resided there.
translations.idiomatic: Crown Prince Zhuangwen later occupied it as well.

sentences.zh: 光宗為太子，孝宗謂輔臣曰：「今後東宮不須創建，朕宮中宮殿，多所不禦，可移修之。」

translations.literal: When Guangzong was crown prince, Xiaozong said to his ministers: "Henceforth the Eastern Palace need not be newly built; within my palace many halls go unused—we can move and refurbish them.
translations.idiomatic: When Guangzong was heir, Xiaozong told his ministers: "There is no need to build a new Eastern Palace. I have halls sitting idle—refit those instead.

sentences.zh: 自是皆不別建。

translations.literal: From then on none were separately built.
translations.idiomatic: After that, no separate Eastern Palace was ever built.

sentences.zh: 淳熙二年，始創射堂一，為遊藝之所，圃中有榮觀玉淵清賞等堂、鳳山樓，皆宴息之地也。

translations.literal: In the 2nd year of Chunxi, one archery hall was first established as a place for leisurely arts; within the garden were Rongguan, Yuyuan Qingshang and other halls, and Fengshan Tower—all places for feasting and repose.
translations.idiomatic: In Chunxi 2 (1175), an archery hall opened as a recreation space; the garden also held Rongguan, Jade Pool Clear Viewing, and Fengshan Tower—all retreats for leisure.

sentences.zh: 幕殿，即《周官》大、小次也。

translations.literal: The tent hall—that is, the great and small resting places in the Offices of Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: The curtained hall corresponded to the great and small resting pavilions described in the Offices of Zhou.

sentences.zh: 東都時，郊壇大次謂之青城，祀前一日宿齋詣焉。

translations.literal: In Eastern Capital times, the great resting place at the suburban altar was called Qingcheng; on the day before the sacrifice one fasted and lodged there.
translations.idiomatic: At the Eastern Capital, the suburban altar's main pavilion was called Qingcheng—the emperor fasted there the eve of sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 其制，中有二殿，外有六門：前曰泰禋，後曰拱極，東曰祥曦，西曰景曜，東偏曰承和，西偏曰迎禧。

translations.literal: Its form: within were two halls; without were six gates: front called Taiyin, rear called Gongji, east called Xiangxi, west called Jingyao, east flank called Chenghe, west flank called Yingxi.
translations.idiomatic: It contained two halls and six outer gates: Taiyin front, Gongji rear, Xiangxi east, Jingyao west, Chenghe on the east flank, Yingxi on the west.

sentences.zh: 大殿曰端誠，便殿曰熙成。

translations.literal: The great hall was called Duancheng; the informal hall was called Xicheng.
translations.idiomatic: The main hall was Duancheng; the side hall, Xicheng.

sentences.zh: 中興後，以事天尚質，屢詔郊壇不得建齋宮，惟設幕屋而已。

translations.literal: After the Restoration, because serving Heaven valued plainness, edicts repeatedly forbade building fasting palaces at the suburban altar—only tent structures were set up.
translations.idiomatic: After the restoration, repeated edicts banned permanent fasting halls at the suburban altar—Heaven's rites should stay spare; only curtain shelters would do.

sentences.zh: 其制，架木而以葦為障，上下四旁周以幄帟，以象宮室，謂之幕殿。

translations.literal: Its form: a wooden frame with reeds as screens; above, below, and on all four sides enclosed with curtains and awnings to resemble palace chambers—called a tent hall.
translations.idiomatic: These were timber frames screened with reed matting, draped on every side with curtains to mimic palace rooms—the curtained hall.

sentences.zh: 及行事，又於壇所設小次。

translations.literal: When performing the rites, a small resting place was also set up at the altar site.
translations.idiomatic: On the day of the rite, a small shelter was erected at the altar itself.

sentences.zh: 大、小次之外，又有望祭殿，遇雨則行事於中。

translations.literal: Beyond the great and small resting places, there was also a hall for rain-offering sacrifices; when it rained the rites were performed within it.
translations.idiomatic: Beyond the main and secondary shelters stood a rain ceremony hall—if weather turned, the rites moved indoors.

sentences.zh: 東都時為瓦屋五間，周圍重廊。

translations.literal: In Eastern Capital times it was a tiled building of five bays, with double corridors all around.
translations.idiomatic: At the Eastern Capital this had been a five-bay tiled hall ringed by covered corridors.

sentences.zh: 中興後，惟設葦屋，蓋仿清廟茅屋之制也。

translations.literal: After the Restoration, only reed-thatched structures were set up—likely imitating the thatched-hall system of the Pure Temple.
translations.idiomatic: After the restoration, only reed-thatched shelters were used—deliberately echoing the thatched Pure Temple of antiquity.

sentences.zh: 臣庶室屋制度。

translations.literal: Regulations for chambers and houses of officials and commoners.
translations.idiomatic: Dwellings of Officials and Commoners.

sentences.zh: 宰相以下治事之所曰省、曰台、曰部、曰寺、曰監、曰院，在外監司、州郡曰衙。

translations.literal: From grand counselor downward, places for conducting affairs were called departments, bureaus, ministries, directorates, commissions, and institutes; supervisory commissioners and prefectures outside were called yamen.
translations.idiomatic: Grand counselors and below worked in departments, bureaus, ministries, directorates, commissions, and academies; regional commissioners and prefectures were known as yamen.

sentences.zh: 在外稱衙而在內之公卿、大夫、士不稱者，按唐制，天子所居曰衙，故臣下不得稱。

translations.literal: Those called yamen outside but whose titled nobles, grandees, and gentlemen inside did not use the term—according to Tang institutions, where the Son of Heaven resided was called yamen, hence subjects could not use the term.
translations.idiomatic: Only outsiders called their offices yamen; inner-court officials did not—a Tang holdover, since yamen properly named the emperor's own quarters and subjects could not claim it.

sentences.zh: 後在外藩鎮亦僭曰衙，遂為臣下通稱。

translations.literal: Later outer frontier garrisons also presumptuously called themselves yamen, and it became the common designation of subjects.
translations.idiomatic: Later regional militaries usurped the term too, until yamen became ordinary officials' shorthand everywhere.

sentences.zh: 今帝居雖不曰衙，而在內省部、寺監之名，則仍唐舊也。

translations.literal: Now although the imperial residence is not called yamen, the names of inner departments, ministries, and commissions still follow Tang precedent.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's residence no longer bears the name, yet inner ministries and directorates still carry Tang-era titles.

sentences.zh: 然亦在內者為尊者避，在外者遠君無嫌歟？

translations.literal: Yet is it also that those within avoid the honored one, while those outside, distant from the ruler, have no cause for scruple?
translations.idiomatic: Was this reverence for the sovereign within the palace—and indifference, or freedom from taboo, beyond it?

sentences.zh: 私居，執政、親王曰府，餘官曰宅，庶民曰家。

translations.literal: Private residences: chief ministers and imperial princes were called mansions; remaining officials were called houses; common people were called homes.
translations.idiomatic: In private life, chief ministers and princes lived in fu mansions, other officials in zhai residences, commoners in jia households.

sentences.zh: 諸道府公門得施戟，若私門則爵位穹顯經恩賜者，許之。

translations.literal: At circuit and prefecture public gates halberds could be displayed; for private gates, only those whose rank was exalted and elevated and had received grace by bestowal were permitted.
translations.idiomatic: Prefecture and circuit government gates could mount ceremonial halberds; private gates only if rank and imperial favor warranted it.

sentences.zh: 在內官不設，亦避君也。

translations.literal: Inner-court officials did not set them up—again avoiding the ruler.
translations.idiomatic: Inner-court officials mounted none—for the same reason of deference to the throne.

sentences.zh: 凡公宇，棟施瓦獸，門設梐枑。

translations.literal: Generally in government office buildings, roof ridges bore tile beasts; gates were fitted with barrier posts.
translations.idiomatic: Government buildings sported ridge beasts on the eaves and ceremonial barrier posts at the gates.

sentences.zh: 諸州正牙門及城門，並施鴟尾，不得施拒鵲。

translations.literal: At the main tooth gate and city gates of the various prefectures, owl-tail ornaments were to be applied; magpie-tail ornaments were not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: Prefectural main gates and city gates were to bear owl-tail ridge ornaments; magpie-tail ornaments were forbidden.

sentences.zh: 六品以上宅舍，許作烏頭門。

translations.literal: For residential compounds of the sixth rank and above, black-headed gates were permitted.
translations.idiomatic: Officials of the sixth rank and above might erect black-headed gates at their residences.

sentences.zh: 父祖舍宅有者，子孫許仍之。

translations.literal: If a father or grandfather's residence already had one, descendants were permitted to retain it.
translations.idiomatic: Where a forebear's house already possessed such a gate, descendants might keep it.

sentences.zh: 凡民庶家，不得施重栱、藻井及五色文采為飾，仍不得四鋪飛簷。

translations.literal: Commoners' households were not permitted heavy bracket sets, coffered ceilings, or five-colored patterned ornamentation as decoration, nor four-layer flying eaves.
translations.idiomatic: Common households might not use heavy bracketing, coffered ceilings, polychrome patterned decoration, or four-tier flying eaves.

sentences.zh: 庶人舍屋，許五架，門一間兩廈而已。

translations.literal: Commoners' dwellings were permitted five roof frames, with a gate of one bay and two side wings only.
translations.idiomatic: Commoners' houses were limited to five roof frames and a single-bay gate with two side wings.
